Seeking shade when the temperature rises
correctAnswer: Seeking shade when the temperature rises
explanation: Behavioral thermoregulation includes seeking shade or shelter.

text: Industries in the medicine sector use glucose oxidase in clinistix strips for
options: restoring blood supply to area of heart muscle.
detecting toxic metabolites in the blood.
easy diagnosis of diabetes by examining a urine sample.
correctAnswer: easy diagnosis of diabetes by examining a urine sample.
explanation: Glucose oxidase detects glucose in urine for diabetes screening.

text: In the systematic naming of enzymes, assume an enzyme is designated as EC 3.4.11.1. Which of the following correctly describes this enzyme?
options: 11 - gives a sub-subclass to which the enzyme belongs.
4 - shows to which main class the enzyme belongs.
3 - indicates a subclass to which the enzyme belongs.
correctAnswer: 11 - gives a sub-subclass to which the enzyme belongs.
explanation: In EC numbers, the third number indicates sub-subclass.

text: Which one of the following sentences is correct about apo-enzymes? They are
options: cofactors that give an enzyme its catalytic activity.
proteins that combine with cofactors to form active enzymes.
organic molecules and many are derived from vitamins.
inorganic molecules that bind loosely with the cofactors.
correctAnswer: proteins that combine with cofactors to form active enzymes.
explanation: Apoenzymes are the protein portion requiring cofactors for activity.

text: How does a competitive inhibitor affect an enzyme catalyzed reaction? By
options: denaturing the active site of the enzyme
producing conformational change of the enzyme
binding to the allosteric site of the enzyme
blocking the active site of the enzyme
correctAnswer: blocking the active site of the enzyme
explanation: Competitive inhibitors compete for the active site.

text: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the movement of materials in plants?
options: Passive transport can takes place in the phloem.
The transport of organic materials is due to transpiration.
Water is transported in dead tissue.
Active transport can take place in the xylem.
correctAnswer: Water is transported in dead tissue.
explanation: Xylem vessels are dead cells transporting water.

text: What will happen if an agriculture extension worker injects gibberellins into a dwarf plant? The
explanation: Gibberellins primarily stimulate stem elongation.

text: A biologist collected two types of seeds (SA and SB) from the field and sowed them in moist soils enriched with nutrients. Then, he recorded his observations. Which one of the following is correct about the observations of the biologist?
options: Both SA and SB are of monocots.
SA is of a monocot, while SB is of a dicot.
Both SA and SB are of dicots.
SA is of a dicot, while SB is of a monocot.
correctAnswer: SA is of a dicot, while SB is of a monocot.
explanation: SA shows epigeal germination (dicot), SB shows hypogeal (monocot).

text: Which one of the following sentences correctly describes the properties of water? It
options: contracts when it freezes and ice acts as an insulator.
takes low energy to change into vapor.
allows all light wavelengths to pass through its various depths.
requires high amount of energy to heat up.
correctAnswer: requires high amount of energy to heat up.
explanation: Water has high specific heat capacity.

text: In animal cells, glycogen is hydrolyzed quickly to release glucose for respiration. This is due to the presence of several
explanation: Glycogen phosphorylase and other enzymes rapidly break glycogen.

text: Which of the following is an Ethiopian endemic plant?
explanation: This answer is questionable. 'Bahir zaf' in Amharic usually refers to Eucalyptus species, which are actually native to Australia and were introduced to Ethiopia. Truly endemic Ethiopian plants include Erythrina brucei and certain species of Lobelia. There might be a specific local species of tree called 'Bahir zaf' that is endemic, but Eucalyptus is definitely not endemic to Ethiopia.

text: When a biologist shares her research findings with other fellow biologists, she is
explanation: Sharing findings constitutes results reporting.

text: Walia ibex is an endemic animal species in Ethiopia which is found in
explanation: Walia ibex inhabit the Simien Mountains.

text: Choose the incorrect one from the following statements
options: Fishery science covers the processes from cultivating of fishes to supplying them on market
Fishery science integrates the behaviors, ecology and population abundance predicting methods
Various ecology adaptations allowed the fishes to have most diversity among others vertebrates
Dorsal and anal fins help fish to walk in water just as of fore and hind legs of other animals
correctAnswer: Dorsal and anal fins help fish to walk in water just as of fore and hind legs of other animals
explanation: The incorrect statement is 'Dorsal and anal fins help fish to walk in water just as of fore and hind legs of other animals.' This is incorrect because dorsal and anal fins primarily provide stability and control during swimming, not locomotion like legs. Pectoral and pelvic fins are more analogous to limbs.

text: Identify the correct statement regarding translation in eukaryotic cells.
options: The helicase enzyme begins to unwind a section of DNA.
The polymerase assembles free RNA nucleotides into a chain.
The first two codons of the mRNA enter the ribosome.
The RNA polymerase moves along the antisense strand.
correctAnswer: The first two codons of the mRNA enter the ribosome.
explanation: During translation initiation, the ribosome assembles around the mRNA start codon (AUG) and the second codon. The initiator tRNA carrying methionine binds to the P-site of the ribosome at the start codon, and the process begins.

text: Which one of the following sentences is correct about mitosis?
options: It is the division of sex cells resulting in identical daughter cells.
It produces four different daughter cells from a single cell.
It is the division of somatic cells to make identical daughter cells.
It produces half number of chromosomes from the original cell.
correctAnswer: It is the division of somatic cells to make identical daughter cells.
explanation: Mitosis produces two genetically identical somatic cells.

text: A cross between pea plants having heterozygous genotype (Rr) has been made. Which of the following is correct about the offspring according to the Mendelian inheritance? The genotypic probability of getting
explanation: A heterozygous cross yields 25% RR, 50% Rr, and 25% rr.

text: Which one of the following events happens during carbon cycle? Carbon dioxide is
options: transferred from plants to animals by their feeding relationship.
absorbed from air when microbes decompose plants and animals.
removed from the air by animals during respiration.
returned into the air by plants during photosynthesis.
correctAnswer: transferred from plants to animals by their feeding relationship.
explanation: Carbon (in the form of organic carbon compounds, not CO2) is transferred from plants to animals when animals consume plants. Plants fix CO2 during photosynthesis into organic compounds, which are then transferred up the food chain.

text: Which one of the following sentences explains the lock-and-key model of enzyme action?
options: The attached substrate- the enzyme complex enters into a transition state.
The model explains enzyme inhibition in a complete manner.
The shapes of the substrate is complementary to the active site.
The attachment of substrate to an enzyme produces a conformational change.
correctAnswer: The shapes of the substrate is complementary to the active site.
explanation: The lock-and-key model emphasizes shape complementarity.

text: Which one of the following leaf structures is correctly matched with its function?
options: Palisade mesophyll - the main photosynthetic tissue of the leaf
Waxy cuticle - controls the entry of carbon dioxide into the leaf
Guard cells - have lots of air space and gas exchange area of the leaf
Spongy mesophyll - helps to prevent water loss from the leaf
correctAnswer: Palisade mesophyll - the main photosynthetic tissue of the leaf
explanation: Palisade mesophyll contains most chloroplasts for photosynthesis.

text: In the aerobic cellular respiration
options: Krebs cycle takes place in the cytoplasm.
glycolysis takes place in the mitochondria.
electron transport chain takes place in the cytoplasm.
pyruvate enters into the mitochondria for further stages.
correctAnswer: pyruvate enters into the mitochondria for further stages.
explanation: Pyruvate moves into mitochondria for oxidative processes.

text: Which of the following is the most advanced and recent event in the history of cell biology?
options: Discovery of the double-helix structure of DNA
Enovation of the first scanning electron microscope
explanation: Human genome sequencing (completed 2003) is the most recent among these milestones.

text: Which one of the following is an example of in-sight learning?
options: Salivation of a dog when a bell was rung in the absence of food, which was paired with the conditioned stimulus.
Use of boxes, after several trials, by a chimpanzee placed in an enclosed area to obtain bananas placed on the top of an enclosure.
Exhibition of modifications of natural behaviors of guide dogs, horses or zoo animals to desired behaviors.
Lack of response from a lady, which sat in a shop in which a strong deodorant was continuously released from a can.
correctAnswer: Use of boxes, after several trials, by a chimpanzee placed in an enclosed area to obtain bananas placed on the top of an enclosure.
explanation: This actually isn't a clear example of insight learning. True insight learning involves a sudden understanding of a problem without trial and error, but this example describes the chimpanzee using boxes 'after several trials,' which suggests trial and error learning. A better example of insight learning would be if the chimpanzee immediately stacked boxes to reach the banana without previous attempts. Option A describes classical conditioning, option C describes operant conditioning, and option D describes habituation.

text: Which one of the following is true about plant cells? They have
options: vacuole which controls all activities of the cell.
chloroplast which is filled with sap, liquids and minerals.
cell wall which gives support and strengthen to the cell.
correctAnswer: cell wall which gives support and strengthen to the cell.
explanation: Plant cell walls provide structural support.

text: Which one of the following is correct about human food digestion?
options: The stomach physically breaks down the ingested food.
Mouth use protease enzyme to breakdown proteins.
Large intestine is the site of lipid hydrolysis.
The small intestine is site of absorption of digested molecules.
correctAnswer: The small intestine is site of absorption of digested molecules.
explanation: Most nutrient absorption occurs in the small intestine.

text: About 3 million years ago the Isthmus of Panama separated the shrimp population of the Caribbean Sea and created two populations of shrimps, one on either side of the isthmus. They still look remarkably similar, but they do not interbreed with each other. Which type of isolation is described by this scenario?
explanation: The scenario describes geographical isolation where a physical barrier (the Isthmus of Panama) separated the population.

text: Which one of the following sentences is correct about the activities of the heart?
options: The noise of heartbeat one hears through a stethoscope is the sound of valves.
As the heart beats blood travels through the arteries with a uniform pressure.
Diastole is when the heart muscles contract and force the blood out.
Systole is when the heart muscles relax and it fills with blood.
correctAnswer: The noise of heartbeat one hears through a stethoscope is the sound of valves.
explanation: The sound heard through a stethoscope is indeed the sound of heart valves opening and closing.

text: During culturing micro-organisms, all of the following activities are important EXCEPT
options: tilting the lid of the Petri dish during inoculation.
adding distilled water to a sterilized agar.
transferring target micro-organisms into an agar medium.
correctAnswer: adding distilled water to a sterilized agar.
explanation: Adding water to sterilized agar would contaminate it; the agar should already contain the proper moisture content.

text: Which one of the following diseases can be caused by more than one type of microorganisms?
explanation: Gastroenteritis can be caused by various viruses, bacteria, or parasites.

text: Which one of the following diseases is correctly explained with its causes or symptoms?
options: Syphilis is caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
Gonorrhoea has a burning sensation symptom while urinating.
Gonorrhoea is caused by Treponema pallidum.
Syphilis has sore ulceration on the genitals as a symptom.
correctAnswer: Syphilis has sore ulceration on the genitals as a symptom.
explanation: Syphilis is characterized by chancre sores (painless ulcerations) on the genitals and is caused by Treponema pallidum. Gonorrhea is caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae and has symptoms including burning during urination.

text: Which one of the following statements is correct about the description of the cell theory?
options: Schleiden and Schwann stated that all cells come from pre-existing cells.
Virchow stated that cell is the unit of structure, physiology and organization of living things.
Modern cell theory states that cells contain hereditary information that passes from cell to cell.
Spontaneous generation theory states that all cells have basically different chemical composition.
correctAnswer: Modern cell theory states that cells contain hereditary information that passes from cell to cell.
explanation: The modern cell theory includes the principle that cells contain DNA/genetic information that is passed to daughter cells during cell division. However, there are other historical inaccuracies in the options: it was Rudolf Virchow who proposed 'omnis cellula e cellula' (all cells come from pre-existing cells), not Schleiden and Schwann. Schleiden and Schwann established that all organisms are composed of cells. The spontaneous generation theory incorrectly proposed that living organisms could arise from non-living matter.

text: One of the following renowned Ethiopian biologists has discovered a 3.3 million - year - old humanoid child fossil in 2006.
explanation: Dr Zeresenay Alemseged discovered the fossil.

text: Which of the following statements best states the cell theory?
options: Cells can arise spontaneously from non - living matter
Only plant cells can perform photosynthesis
Cells are only found in multicellular organisms
Cells are the basic unit of life
correctAnswer: Cells are the basic unit of life
explanation: The cell theory states that cells are the basic unit of life.

text: If a cell is observed under a microscope and has a large permanent central vacuole, which type of cell is it most likely to be?
explanation: Plant cells typically have a large central vacuole.

text: If a cell is placed in hypertonic solution, what will most likely happen to the cell?
options: It will remain the same size
explanation: In a hypertonic solution, the cell will lose water and shrink.

text: If one of your friends is having a hard time for chewing and crushing food, which type of his teeth is most likely affected?
explanation: Premolars and molars are responsible for crushing and grinding food.

text: A group of grade 9 students is studying the effect of smoking on lung function. They find that smokers have reduced lung capacity compared to non-smokers. What conclusion can they draw from this data?
options: Smoking has no effect on lung capacity
Lung capacity can be improved with exercise, regardless of smoking history
Smoking is likely a contributing factor to reduced lung capacity
All smokers will have the same lung capacity regardless of other factors
correctAnswer: Smoking is likely a contributing factor to reduced lung capacity
explanation: The data suggests that smoking negatively impacts lung capacity.

text: Which one of the following stages of cell division is correctly described in meiosis II?
options: Prophase II - pairs of homologous chromosomes split up
Anaphase II - chromatids from each chromosome separate
Metaphase II - chromosomes pair and exchange segments
Telophase II - two haploid cells are produced
correctAnswer: Anaphase II - chromatids from each chromosome separate
explanation: In Anaphase II, sister chromatids separate, similar to mitotic anaphase.

text: Which one of the following events is an example of a sex influenced trait?
explanation: Pattern baldness is a sex-influenced trait that is more common in males due to hormonal influences.

text: Which of the following processes takes place when lactate is produced?
options: NAD and FAD are regenerated from reduced NAD and FAD.
ATP is produced through oxidative phosphorylation.
Protons accumulation created in the inter-membrane space.
Reduced NAD supplies hydrogen and becomes oxidized itself.
correctAnswer: Reduced NAD supplies hydrogen and becomes oxidized itself.
explanation: In lactate fermentation, NADH is oxidized to NAD+ while reducing pyruvate to lactate.

text: In the scientific name Canis simensis, what does simensis refer to?
explanation: Simensis is the species name in the binomial nomenclature.

text: Which one of the following structures of the photosystem is correctly related with its function?
options: Chlorophyll a - a reaction center molecule
Thylakoid - absorbs blue and red pigments
correctAnswer: Chlorophyll a - a reaction center molecule
explanation: Chlorophyll a is the primary reaction center molecule in photosystems.

text: What happens during the electron transport system of respiration? The
options: four-carbon compound undergoes molecular transformation to generate oxaloacetate.
hydrogen atoms carried by FADH and NADH are released and split into protons and electrons.
citrate losses a carbon atom to form a five-carbon atom compound and CO₂.
five carbon compound is further decarboxylated to form a four-carbon compound.
correctAnswer: hydrogen atoms carried by FADH and NADH are released and split into protons and electrons.
explanation: In the ETC, NADH and FADH2 donate electrons which are split into protons and electrons.

text: During light independent reactions of photosynthesis, glucose is synthesized through
options: synthesis of reduced NADP that provides hydrogen ion
six turns of the Calvin cycle to make one molecule of glucose.
release of hydrogen ions at the electron transport chain.
transmission of electrons to the inside of the thylakoid.
correctAnswer: six turns of the Calvin cycle to make one molecule of glucose.
explanation: The Calvin cycle must turn 6 times to produce one glucose molecule (6 CO2 molecules are fixed).

text: Which one of the following monohybrid crosses can be a test cross?
explanation: A test cross involves crossing with a homozygous recessive (rr) individual to determine the genotype of the other parent.

text: Which of the following is different from the rest with regard to conservation of vegetation?
options: Replanting of land with endemic species
Large scale introduction of exotic plants
correctAnswer: Large scale introduction of exotic plants
explanation: Introducing exotic plants is different from the other conservation methods which focus on native species.

text: In the nervous co-ordination system, which of the following statements explains the synapse? It is a
options: chemical that transmits nerve impulses across the nervous system.
part of the skull that encloses brain for the purpose of protection.
junction between two neurons or a neuron and a muscle.
short term change in the electrical potential on the surface of cells.
correctAnswer: junction between two neurons or a neuron and a muscle.
explanation: A synapse is the junction between neurons or between a neuron and effector cell (muscle/gland).

text: Which of the following eye structures is correctly matched with its function?
options: Pupil - serves as the eye's protective outer layer.
Iris - controls the amount of light entering the eye.
Cornea - provides nutrition to the retina.
Choroid - bends the light into the eye.
correctAnswer: Iris - controls the amount of light entering the eye.
explanation: The iris controls pupil size and thus regulates light entering the eye.

text: In the CAM photosynthetic pathway,
options: malate is stored in the mesophyll cells during the day.
glucose is synthesized in the bundle sheath cell during night.
ATP and NADPH are produced during the night.
the C4 stage and the Calvin cycle are separated in time.
correctAnswer: the C4 stage and the Calvin cycle are separated in time.
explanation: CAM plants separate carbon fixation (night) and Calvin cycle (day) temporally rather than spatially.

text: Schizogony is a form of asexual reproduction in protozoa which is common in Sporozoa. How do Sporozoa cells divide in schizogony?
options: Nucleus divides multiple times before the cell divides.
Cell divides unevenly without nuclear division.
Cell divides evenly to form two new cells.
The cell divides longitudinally into two.
correctAnswer: Nucleus divides multiple times before the cell divides.
explanation: In schizogony, the nucleus undergoes multiple divisions before the cell divides.

text: Which one of the following sentences describes a virus? It
explanation: Viruses are acellular infectious agents that require host cells to replicate.

text: Which subclass of gymnospermopsida is extinct?
explanation: Pteridospermae (seed ferns) is an extinct subclass of gymnosperms that had characteristics of both ferns and seed plants. They flourished during the Carboniferous and Permian periods but became extinct by the end of the Mesozoic era. The other subclasses listed (Gnetae, Coniferae, and Cycadae) have extant representatives.

text: During cell cycle, in which of the following phase does a cell double its chromosomes?
explanation: The S-phase (Synthesis phase) is when DNA replication occurs, effectively doubling the chromosomes. This phase is part of interphase, occurring between G1 and G2 phases. During metaphase, chromosomes are already doubled and are aligned at the cell's equator, while G1 and G2 are growth phases with no DNA replication.

text: River blindness is the name given to disease caused by
explanation: Onchocerca volvulus is the causative agent of river blindness (onchocerciasis). This filarial nematode is transmitted by blackflies (Simulium species) that breed in fast-flowing rivers, hence the name 'river blindness'. The adult worms produce microfilariae that migrate to the skin and eyes, causing inflammation that can lead to blindness.

text: Which one of the following is harmful insect?
explanation: None of the listed insects are generally considered harmful. Lac insects (Kerria lacca) produce lac, which is used in various products including shellac. Honey bees (Apis species) produce honey and are essential pollinators. Silkworms (Bombyx mori) produce silk. These are all economically beneficial insects, not harmful pests.

text: The binomial system of naming developed by Linnaeus comprises two names. Which hierarchical groups are used?
explanation: Binomial nomenclature uses the genus and species names (e.g., Homo sapiens).

text: Which one of the following is a feature of Octopi and squid in phylum mollusca? They have
options: segmented body with head and thorax.
hard muscular foot with a hard body.
explanation: Cephalopods like octopi and squid have the most developed brains among invertebrates.

text: The breeding mechanism that improves the performance of animals or plants using particular traits is
explanation: Selective breeding involves choosing organisms with desired traits for reproduction.

text: The two reverse processes that play a significant role in absorbing and releasing carbon dioxide, respectively are
explanation: Photosynthesis absorbs CO2 while respiration releases it.

text: In which sterilization method are items to be sterilized kept in the chamber and exposed to free-flowing steam at 100ºC for 20 minutes, for each of the three consecutive days?
explanation: Tyndallization is a method of sterilization using steam.

text: Which one of the following diseases increases the likelihood of contracting HIV?
explanation: Chancroid, caused by Haemophilus ducreyi, produces genital ulcers that compromise the skin barrier and increase HIV transmission risk by providing entry points for the virus and recruiting CD4+ T cells (HIV targets) to the area.

text: Which one of the following adaptations is important for survival of polar bear in very cold environments? Having
explanation: Blubber (thick layer of fat) provides insulation against extreme cold temperatures by retaining body heat. Polar bears have up to 4 inches of blubber under their skin, which is crucial for survival in Arctic conditions.

text: Which one of the following plant species is endemic to Ethiopia?
explanation: Guitzoia abyssinica (Niger seed) is native to Ethiopia.

text: Which one of the following national parks of Ethiopia is declared as the world's heritage site and comprises endemic animals like Walia ibex?
explanation: Simien Mountains National Park is a UNESCO site home to the Walia ibex.

text: A mother milks her cow every morning and the milk usually forms curd after three days. What is the first step to investigate why this change happens?
options: Take action to prevent the milk from curdling
Read scientific articles about the reason for curdling of milk
Formulate hypothesis about the reason for milk curdling
Ask a question why the milk forms curd
correctAnswer: Ask a question why the milk forms curd
explanation: The scientific method begins with asking a question.

text: Which one of the following mechanisms of microbial control is antisepsis?
options: Applying a solution of 5% bleaches to examining table
Boiling food utensils used by a sick person
Immersing thermometers in an isopropyl alcohol solution between uses.
Preparing the skin before surgical incisions with iodine compounds
correctAnswer: Preparing the skin before surgical incisions with iodine compounds
explanation: Antisepsis involves using chemicals to eliminate pathogens on living tissues.

text: In water, phospholipids become organized into a bilayer. In this configuration, which part of the bilayer faces towards the water?
explanation: The hydrophilic phosphate heads face outward toward water, while hydrophobic tails face inward.

text: Which one of the following is correct about the action of apoenzymes and coenzymes?
options: Coenzymes bind with cofactors to form an active enzyme.
Apoenzymes bind with enzymes to give catalytic activity.
Both apoenzymes and coenzymes combine with cofactors to form a non-active enzyme.
Coenzymes bind with apoenzymes to give catalytic activity.
correctAnswer: Coenzymes bind with apoenzymes to give catalytic activity.
explanation: An apoenzyme is the protein portion of an enzyme without its non-protein component. A coenzyme is a non-protein organic molecule that works with the apoenzyme to form a complete, catalytically active holoenzyme. Examples of coenzymes include NAD+, NADP+, FAD, and coenzyme A.

text: A student focused a slide of an onion epidermal cell on pre-estimated width of 2 millimeter field of view under a microscope. What will be the width of each individual cell if you count 8 cells that fit to the field of view during your observation?
explanation: To find the width of each cell, divide the total field width by the number of cells: 2mm ÷ 8 cells = 0.25mm per cell. This calculation assumes cells are of equal size across the field of view.

text: Which one of the following statements is correct about the differences between eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells? Prokaryotic cells have
options: membrane bound organelles whereas eukaryotic cells don't have it.
small ribosomes whereas eukaryotic cells have large ribosomes.
cell wall whereas eukaryotic cells don't have cell wall.
division of labor whereas eukaryotic cells don't have it.
correctAnswer: small ribosomes whereas eukaryotic cells have large ribosomes.
explanation: Prokaryotic ribosomes (70S) are smaller than eukaryotic ribosomes (80S).

text: Which one of the following statements shows the future promise of biological sciences?
options: Finding alternative living place for human population
Using stem cells to repair damaged organs and grow new organ
Finding the adaptation mechanism of plant in new condition
Advising the government on how to conserve environment
correctAnswer: Using stem cells to repair damaged organs and grow new organ
explanation: Stem cell therapy represents a major frontier in medical biology.

text: If an enzyme is named as "EC 3.4.11.1." in a systematic naming, what does the number "3" represents? It represents the
options: sub-subclass of an enzyme in relation to its protein nature.
ultra-subclass of an enzyme that is related to the place where they act.
sub-class of an enzyme in relation to the source from where it was discovered.
main class of an enzyme which indicates the type of reaction it catalyses.
correctAnswer: main class of an enzyme which indicates the type of reaction it catalyses.
explanation: The first number in EC classification indicates the main reaction type (hydrolases in this case).

text: In the lock-and-key model of enzymatic action, the activation energy is lowered through
options: provision of alternative pathway for the reaction.
straining of the substrate molecules bound to the active site.
permanent modification of the active site of the enzyme.
correctAnswer: provision of alternative pathway for the reaction.
explanation: Enzymes provide an alternative reaction pathway with lower activation energy.

text: Which one of the following organic molecules has ester bonds in its molecular structure?
explanation: Triglycerides have ester bonds linking fatty acids to glycerol.

text: Which one of the following is an example of a catabolic process?
explanation: Cellular respiration is a catabolic process that breaks down glucose to release energy.

text: Which one of the following statements is true about female genital mutilation? It
explanation: FGM carries serious health risks including infection, despite cultural justifications.

text: Why are root hairs efficient in uptake of water from the soil? Because they
options: anchor the plant to the ground.
have high surface area to volume ratio.
correctAnswer: have high surface area to volume ratio.
explanation: Root hairs maximize absorption surface while being small enough for close soil contact.

text: A farmer sowed cotton seeds in a farm land which fulfills the optimum conditions for germination. After a few days, he observed the newly growing seedlings. Which of the following statements is correct about the farmer's observation? The
options: growth of plumule above the soil surface
remaining of the cotyledon below the ground.
growth of plumule without forming a hook
correctAnswer: growth of plumule above the soil surface
explanation: Cotton shows epigeal germination where hypocotyl elongates, raising cotyledons above ground.

text: What is the justification for feeling warm while sweating a lot in a very humid condition?
options: The lower rate of evaporation of water from the skin surfaces
Closure of the glands in the epidermal layer of the skin
An increase in metabolic rate as temperature increases
Unequal distribution of ions on membrane of cells
correctAnswer: The lower rate of evaporation of water from the skin surfaces
explanation: High humidity reduces sweat evaporation, impairing cooling.

text: Which one of the following alternatives contains only protein rich cereals?
options: Red kidney pens, maize and white pea
White kidney pens, red kidney pens and chickpea
Wheat, red kidney pens and sesame
correctAnswer: White kidney pens, red kidney pens and chickpea
explanation: Beans (kidney beans) and chickpeas are protein-rich legumes.

text: What is the main function of the dermis of the skin?
options: Prevention of the entry of pathogens
Synthesis of hair and nail proteins
explanation: Dermis contains sweat glands, blood vessels etc. crucial for thermoregulation.

text: Which of the following is the correct description of hormones? They are chemical messengers that
options: transmit message faster than the nerve system.
targets only the site of secretion.
are produced in glands that contain ducts.
explanation: Hormones regulate diverse physiological processes throughout the body.

text: Which of the following statements is true regarding non-cyclic photophosphorylation?
options: It generates oxygen as a byproduct
It occurs in the stroma of the chloroplast
correctAnswer: It generates oxygen as a byproduct
explanation: Non-cyclic photophosphorylation produces ATP, NADPH, and oxygen.

text: How does photosynthesis contribute to mitigating global warming?
options: By producing oxygen as a byproduct
By absorbing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere
correctAnswer: By absorbing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere
explanation: Photosynthesis absorbs CO2, a greenhouse gas, helping to mitigate global warming.

text: In which parts of the cell do the reactions of cellular respiration occur?
explanation: Cellular respiration occurs in the cytosol and mitochondria.

text: Which statement shows the correct comparison between the Lamarek's and Darwin's theory of evolution?
options: Lamarek believed in the development of new traits due to variation while Darwin believed in their occurrence due to use and disuse of organs.
Darwin recognized the origin of species was through mutation while Lamarek believed it was through effect of the environment.
Lamarek believed the gradual occurrence of changes while Darwin believed in the immediate change of species.
Darwin claimed that variation is heritable while Lamarek considers variation as acquired traits.
correctAnswer: Darwin claimed that variation is heritable while Lamarek considers variation as acquired traits.
explanation: Key difference: Darwin's heritable variations vs Lamarck's inheritance of acquired characteristics.

text: Which one of the following statements correctly explains the genetic drift? It is a change in allele frequency due to
options: non- random mating of individuals in a population.
relocation of species into other areas.
explanation: Genetic drift is random fluctuation of allele frequencies, especially in small populations.

text: Which one of the following statements correctly describes bacteria? They are
explanation: Bacteria are unicellular prokaryotes.

text: As compared to non- cyclic photophosphorylation, the cyclic photophosphorylation uses the
options: photosystem I as the last electron acceptor.
photosystem I to produce ATP and reduced NADP in the stroma.
hydrolysis of water to replace electrons lost from photosystem II.
photosystem II as the first electron donor to NADP.
correctAnswer: photosystem I as the last electron acceptor.
explanation: Cyclic photophosphorylation involves only PS I, with electrons returning to it.

text: Which one of the following descriptions about glycolysis is correct? It is a process
options: of producing acetyl CoA from pyruvate by releasing CO₂.
that produces a net of 4 ATP through substrate level phosphorylation.
of breaking down of a glucose molecule to two pyruvates.
that takes place in the cytosol with high demand of oxygen.
correctAnswer: of breaking down of a glucose molecule to two pyruvates.
explanation: Glycolysis splits glucose (6C) into 2 pyruvate (3C) molecules.

text: Which of the following statements is CORRECT regarding Tape worms?
options: They have a complete digestive system
Have complete lifecycle, which involves at least two hosts
Live in mutualistic association with host
explanation: Tape worms absorb nutrients directly from their host. They also typically have a complex lifecycle involving multiple hosts, but the primary characteristic mentioned in the correct answer is about their feeding mechanism.

text: Which of the following statements about class monocotyledon plant is true?
options: The embryo has two seed leaves
In general, monocots reach great sizes
explanation: Monocots typically have leaves with parallel veins.

text: What role do receptors play in the homeostasis process?
options: They detect stimuli and send information to the brain.
They adjust body conditions back towards the set point.
They regulate the body's response to stimuli.
correctAnswer: They detect stimuli and send information to the brain.
explanation: Receptors detect stimuli and relay information for homeostasis.

text: What is the quaternary structure of a protein?
options: The folding pattern of the polypeptide chain.
explanation: The quaternary structure refers to how multiple polypeptide chains interact.

text: What is the function of hydrogen ions produced from the oxidation of NADH and FADH2 during oxidative phosphorylation?
options: It is used to spin the rotor of ATP synthase
It is used to reduce molecular oxygen
It is used to regenerate FAD and NAD+
It is used to create an electrochemical gradient
correctAnswer: It is used to create an electrochemical gradient
explanation: Hydrogen ions (protons) create an electrochemical gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane. This gradient stores potential energy, which is then used by ATP synthase as protons flow back through it, causing the enzyme's rotor to spin and catalyze ATP synthesis in a process known as chemiosmosis.

text: In the electron transport chain, the NADH and FADH2 formed during glycolysis, link reaction, and citric acid cycle give up their electrons to reduce molecular O2 to:
explanation: Electrons from NADH and FADH2 reduce O2 to form water.

text: What is the most widely accepted definition of evolution?
options: The process by which organisms develop new traits in response to environmental challenges
The change in genetic composition of a population over successive generations
The creation of new species through genetic engineering
The belief that all species were created spontaneously
correctAnswer: The change in genetic composition of a population over successive generations
explanation: Evolution is defined as changes in genetic composition over generations.

text: Who conducted the famous experiment in 1953 that simulated early Earth conditions to test the origins of life?
explanation: Stanley Miller's experiment demonstrated the possible origins of life.

text: Which of the following best describes the concept of 'survival of the fittest' in the context of natural selection?
options: The individuals best adapted to their environment are more likely to reproduce.
All individuals have an equal chance of survival.
Fitness is determined solely by physical strength.
correctAnswer: The individuals best adapted to their environment are more likely to reproduce.
explanation: 'Survival of the fittest' refers to reproductive success based on adaptation.

text: How did Lamarck's theory of evolution differ from Darwin's theory?
options: Lamarck believed in natural selection; Darwin did not.
Lamarck proposed that traits acquired during an organism's lifetime could be passed to offspring, while Darwin focused on natural selection.
Both theories suggest that species do not change over time.
Lamarck's theory was based on genetic evidence; Darwin's was not.
correctAnswer: Lamarck proposed that traits acquired during an organism's lifetime could be passed to offspring, while Darwin focused on natural selection.
explanation: Lamarck's theory involved inheritance of acquired traits, unlike Darwin's natural selection.

text: Who is known for proposing the theory of inheritance of acquired characters?
explanation: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck proposed the theory of inheritance of acquired characteristics.

text: What do homologous structures indicate about two species?
options: They evolved independently due to similar environmental pressures.
They are adapted to different environments.
explanation: Homologous structures suggest a common evolutionary ancestor.

text: How could you use embryological evidence to support the theory of evolution?
options: By showing that all species have identical embryonic stages.
By proving that similar embryonic features suggest common ancestry among different species.
By providing that embryos develop faster in some species than others.
By comparing adult forms rather than embryonic stages.
correctAnswer: By proving that similar embryonic features suggest common ancestry among different species.
explanation: Similar embryonic features indicate evolutionary relationships.

text: Imagine you are studying a bird species with varying beak sizes. If both very small and very large beaks are advantageous for different food sources, what type of natural selection is this an example of?
explanation: Disruptive selection favors extreme traits over intermediate traits.

text: The importance of stains in microscopic investigations is explained by their effect in
explanation: Stains enhance contrast, making cellular structures more visible under the microscope.

text: What is the key feature of the lock and key model of enzyme-substrate interaction?
options: Enzyme active sites fill in with a substrate to interact through covalent interactions.
The enzyme changes shape to better fit the substrate after binding.
The substrate fits perfectly into the enzyme's active site from the start.
The enzyme does not bind to the substrate at all until the reaction is complete.
correctAnswer: The substrate fits perfectly into the enzyme's active site from the start.
explanation: In the lock and key model, the substrate fits precisely into the enzyme's active site.

text: Which type of inhibition is likely occurring if a molecule that inhibits an enzyme's activity binds to an enzyme active site?
explanation: Competitive inhibition occurs when an inhibitor competes with the substrate for the active site.

text: Which one of the following is paleontological evidence of evolution?
options: The presence of homologous structures in living organisms
Traces of organisms from the remote past
Similarities in the DNA base sequences of different organisms
Similarities in the development of embryos in different organisms
correctAnswer: Traces of organisms from the remote past
explanation: Fossils (traces of past organisms) provide direct evidence of evolutionary changes over time.

text: A more comprehensive definition of biodiversity can be given as the
options: richness, ecological and genetic variability of species.
number of individuals of a species in a given area.
diversity of plants and animals in a given area.
number of individuals of a given animal species.
correctAnswer: richness, ecological and genetic variability of species.
explanation: Biodiversity encompasses species richness, ecological diversity, and genetic diversity.

text: Identify the correct statement about intra-specific competition? It is a competition
options: of two species inhabiting the same ecological area.
that leads to local extinction of the species.
explanation: Intra-specific competition occurs between members of the same species for resources like food, mates, etc.

text: Which one is utterly found in Gram-Negative bacteria?
explanation: Both flagella and pili can be found in Gram-negative bacteria.

text: Which one of the following is correct the composition and level of organizational diversity from bottom to top?
options: Kingdom --> Order --> Class --> Phyla --> Families --> Genera --> Species --> Individual
Genera --> Phyla --> Kingdom --> Order --> Families --> Class --> Species --> Individual
Individual --> Species --> Genera --> Families --> Order --> Class --> Phyla --> Kingdom
Kingdom --> Phyla --> Class --> Order --> Families --> Genera --> Species --> Individual
correctAnswer: Kingdom --> Phyla --> Class --> Order --> Families --> Genera --> Species --> Individual
explanation: The correct order of organizational diversity is from Kingdom to Individual.

text: The term vertebrata is synonymous to;
explanation: Vertebrata is most closely synonymous with Craniata, as both terms refer to animals with a cranium or skull. Chordata is a broader phylum that includes vertebrates as well as other subphyla. Urochordata refers specifically to tunicates, and fish is just one class of vertebrates.

text: Which one of the following is the most diversified microorganism?
explanation: Bacteria are the most diverse group of microorganisms.

text: Which one of the following is not a true fungi?
explanation: Slime molds are not classified as true fungi.

text: Which one of the following is not true about Zygomycetes?
options: They reproduce by hyphae without septa
They are the known contaminants of cereals and vegetables
They are one members of higher fungi
correctAnswer: They are one members of higher fungi
explanation: Zygomycetes are not classified as higher fungi.

text: The names of which two taxa are used in binomial nomenclature?
options: The two lowest units of classification
The two middle units of classification
The highest and the lowest unit of classification
The two highest units of classification
correctAnswer: The two lowest units of classification
explanation: Binomial nomenclature uses genus and species, the two lowest taxonomic ranks.

text: Which theory of the origin of life states that life has no beginning or ending?
explanation: The eternity of life theory proposes life has always existed with no origin point.

text: Select incorrect sentences from the following statements
options: To start up aquaculture, types of species and types of aquacultures must be considered
The electricity and distance from the markets are the determinant for investment in aquaculture
Reproduction mode of fishes include both internal and external fertilization
Integration of aquaculture with others agricultural sectors is called polyculture aquaculture
correctAnswer: Integration of aquaculture with others agricultural sectors is called polyculture aquaculture
explanation: The incorrect statement is that 'Integration of aquaculture with others agricultural sectors is called polyculture aquaculture.' This is actually referred to as integrated agriculture-aquaculture (IAA) systems. Polyculture aquaculture refers to raising multiple species of aquatic organisms together in the same system.

text: Which of the following sentences explains how crossing over brings variation?
options: In meiosis I, there is splitting up of pairs of homologous chromosomes and line up.
In meiosis I, there is exchange of a section of DNA between chromatids.
In meiosis II, homologous chromosomes align themselves independent of other pairs.
In meiosis II, chromatids from each chromosome are separated at random.
correctAnswer: In meiosis I, there is exchange of a section of DNA between chromatids.
explanation: Crossing over occurs during prophase I of meiosis when homologous chromosomes exchange genetic material.

text: In human evolution brain size increased over the courses of evolution. Which alternative contains hominids arranged in an increasing order of brain size?
options: Homo neandertalenxis → Homo erectus → Homo habilis → Homo sapiens
Homo erectus → Homo habilis → Homo neandertalenxis → Homo sapiens
Homo erectus → Homo neandertalenxis → Homo habilis → Homo sapiens
Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Homo neandertalenxis → Homo sapiens
correctAnswer: Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Homo neandertalenxis → Homo sapiens
explanation: The correct increasing order of brain size is: Homo habilis (~600-700cc) → Homo erectus (~900-1100cc) → Homo neanderthalensis (~1400cc) → Homo sapiens (~1350-1400cc). While Neanderthals had slightly larger brains on average than modern humans, the organization and efficiency of the Homo sapiens brain is more advanced.

text: Which one of the following groups of organisms is correctly matched with its phylum?
explanation: Starfish belong to Echinodermata.

text: In the course of evolution, which of the following is true about the human brain?
options: Modern humans have a brain size between 0.7% and 1.0% of their body mass.
Australopithecus have a brain size between 1.8% and 2.3% of their body mass.
The pre-humans brain uses 80% of the resting energy requirement.
Homo sapiens brain uses 25% of the resting energy requirement.
correctAnswer: Homo sapiens brain uses 25% of the resting energy requirement.
explanation: The human brain consumes about 20-25% of basal energy.

text: Which one of the following bacteria produces ammonium ion by forming a symbiotic association with peas and beans?
explanation: Rhizobium forms nitrogen-fixing nodules on legumes like peas and beans, converting atmospheric nitrogen to ammonium.

text: Which one of the following sentences explains the Darwin theory of evolution?
options: Environment changes, creating a need for organism to change.
There is a natural variation in features that are heritable.
New features acquired in lifetime are passed to the offspring.
There is development of new feature in order to survive.
correctAnswer: There is a natural variation in features that are heritable.
explanation: Darwin emphasized heritable variation and natural selection.

text: Comparative anatomy provides evidence of evolution because it
options: looks at structural similarities of organisms.
has remains of animals and plants from the remote past.
has an impression of animal even if the actual parts are missing.
studies the development of the embryos of vertebrates.
correctAnswer: looks at structural similarities of organisms.
explanation: Homologous structures indicate common ancestry.

text: Which one of the following diseases is caused by food poisoning bacteria?
explanation: Salmonellosis is caused by Salmonella bacteria, commonly associated with food poisoning.

text: Which one of the following statements is correct about the binomial nomenclature?
options: The genus name is written in full while the species name is abbreviated.
Both genus and species names are capitalized and italicized when printed.
The first letter of genus name is capitalized while the species name is written in small letters.
The genus name is written in English while the species name is written in Latin.
correctAnswer: The first letter of genus name is capitalized while the species name is written in small letters.
explanation: Binomial nomenclature rules specify capitalizing the genus name and using lowercase for the species name, both italicized.

text: Which one of the following statements correctly describes intra-specific and inter-specific competitions? In intra-specific competition the
options: competition is less severe but in inter-specific competition it is more.
competition is for a few requirements but in inter-specific competition the competition is for all requirements.
competing individuals have similar adaptation but in inter-specific competition the adaptation is different.
competing individuals belong to different species but in inter- specific competition the individuals are of the same species.
correctAnswer: competing individuals have similar adaptation but in inter-specific competition the adaptation is different.
explanation: Intra-specific competition occurs between members of the same species with similar adaptations.

text: Which one of the following is an example of social behavior?
options: Exaggeration of size by fluffing up of feathers
Singing of frogs on spring nights
Caring for offspring that are not one's own
correctAnswer: Caring for offspring that are not one's own
explanation: Alloparenting (caring for others' offspring) is a complex social behavior seen in some species.

text: Which one is correctly spelled considering the handwriting of any scientific names?
explanation: Scientific names follow binomial nomenclature where the genus name (Bacillus) is capitalized and the species name (subtilis) is lowercase. Both are italicized when typed or underlined when handwritten. Therefore, 'Bacillus subtilis' is the correct format.

text: Which one of the following is the neo-Darwinian idea of evolution? Evolutionary changes occur due to
options: natural selection through genetics and behavior.
use and disuse of anatomical structures.
correctAnswer: natural selection through genetics and behavior.
explanation: Neo-Darwinism combines Darwin's natural selection with Mendelian genetics to explain evolution.

text: Which of the following is true concerning the evidences of evolution?
options: Organisms which have little genetic relationship show similar behavior.
Organisms which live in the same area have similar evolutionary history.
Species that are closely related share the most similar DNA sequences.
Species that live in the same geographic area have the same genetic makeup.
correctAnswer: Species that are closely related share the most similar DNA sequences.
explanation: DNA similarity is strong evidence for evolutionary relationships.

text: Which one of the following statements is correct about application of bio-pesticide in agriculture? It
options: uses bacteria and fungi or their metabolites to kill insects.
breakdowns glyphosate by an enzyme introduced into plant cell culture.
produces insect resistant crops through modification of the plant genes using bacterial plasmids.
produces toxic chemicals by crops through modification of their genes.
correctAnswer: uses bacteria and fungi or their metabolites to kill insects.
explanation: Biopesticides are derived from natural materials like bacteria, fungi, plants, or certain minerals. For example, Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) produces proteins toxic to specific insect larvae but harmless to humans and beneficial organisms. Other examples include Beauveria bassiana (fungus) that infects insects, and spinosad (derived from soil bacteria). Unlike chemical pesticides, biopesticides are generally less toxic, more targeted to specific pests, and decompose more quickly, reducing environmental impact.

text: In kingdom animalia, which phylum poisons its prey by tentacles that contain stinging cells?
explanation: Cnidarians (Coelenterata) use cnidocytes (stinging cells) on their tentacles to capture prey.

text: Instinctive behavior
options: is common to all members of a species.
may be modified by new experiences.
correctAnswer: is common to all members of a species.
explanation: Instincts are innate behaviors shared by all members of a species.

text: Bacterial cell wall is unique due to its
explanation: The bacterial cell wall is unique primarily because of its chemical composition, specifically the presence of peptidoglycan (in gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria), which is not found in other organisms.

text: Even though pasteurization is a technique used to heat milk, beer and other foods, it cannot preserve food unspoiled for years because it
options: reduces the nutritional content of the food.
is conducted in containers that are not properly sealed.
uses mild temperature that kills most but not all bacteria.
correctAnswer: uses mild temperature that kills most but not all bacteria.
explanation: Pasteurization uses mild heat to kill most but not all bacteria, allowing some to survive and eventually spoil the food.

text: Which genus of bacteria oxidize hydrogen sulphide to sulphate and make sulphate ions available to be taken by plant roots from the soil?
explanation: Thiobacillus bacteria are chemolithotrophs that obtain energy by oxidizing reduced sulfur compounds (like hydrogen sulfide) to sulfate. This process, called sulfur oxidation, makes sulfate ions available to plants and plays a key role in the sulfur cycle. Desulfovibrio works in the opposite direction, reducing sulfate to hydrogen sulfide.

text: What is the significance of Australopithecus afarensis in the study of human evolution? To confirm
options: evolution of bipedalism before large brains
divergent evolution of Homo erectus from Homo habilis
true common ancestor of chimpanzees and humans
convergent evolution of Homo neanderthalensis and Homo erectus
correctAnswer: evolution of bipedalism before large brains
explanation: A. afarensis (e.g., Lucy) showed bipedalism preceded large brain size in human evolution.

text: What happens if the axon is stimulated? Formation of
options: negative charge in both sides of the axon
positive charge outside of the axon
explanation: Stimulation depolarizes the axon, making the interior temporarily positive during an action potential.

text: With four different bases to work with, there are 64 possible triplet codes, but only 20 amino acids are used to make all the different proteins. This is because the DNA code is
explanation: The genetic code is degenerate (redundant), meaning multiple different codons can encode the same amino acid. For example, the amino acid leucine is coded by six different codons (UUA, UUG, CUU, CUC, CUA, CUG). This redundancy helps minimize the impact of point mutations and is a fundamental feature of the genetic code.

text: Breakdown of the thick spongy wall of the uterus at the end of the menstrual cycle is associated with the
options: decrease in progesterone and estrogen concentration.
increase in oestrogen and progesterone concentration.
correctAnswer: decrease in progesterone and estrogen concentration.
explanation: Menstruation occurs when progesterone and estrogen levels drop, causing endometrial shedding.

text: What type of force is responsible if a stool solution is placed in a centrifuge, spins the tube at high speed and the solid particles are forced to settle down at the bottom?
explanation: In a centrifuge, particles experience an apparent outward force (centrifugal force) as the sample rotates at high speed. This force causes particles to move away from the center of rotation and sediment according to their density, with heavier particles moving furthest from the axis of rotation.

text: Ten percent of attendants of a wedding ceremony were sick just after having lunch at the ceremony. What should a student do first to prove scientifically that the sickness was actually linked to the food eaten at the ceremony? She should
options: give drugs to the sick individuals before they contaminate others.
take food sample to a laboratory and analyze the presence of toxin.
ask herself why ten percent of the attendants were sicked.
take stool sample of the sick individuals and analyze the presence of toxins.
correctAnswer: take food sample to a laboratory and analyze the presence of toxin.
explanation: Food analysis would provide direct evidence of contamination linking illness to the meal.

text: Which property of water prevents ponds from drying during the long dry season? High
explanation: High latent heat means water requires much energy to evaporate, preventing rapid drying.

text: At which stage of the population growth curve is the rate of natality and the rate of mortality are expected to be equal?
explanation: In stationary phase, birth and death rates balance, stabilizing population size.

text: Why Drosophila melanogaster are considered ideal for genetic experiments? Because they
options: have the highest number of chromosomes.
breed and keep in large numbers easily.
complete their life cycle within one month.
correctAnswer: breed and keep in large numbers easily.
explanation: Drosophila's short generation time, easy breeding, and simple care make them ideal genetic models.

text: Which one of the following statements best describes the mechanisms by which meiosis brings about variation? Variation in meiosis is because of
options: variations in the content of the cytoplasm between the cells.
reduction division that leads to haploid cell formation.
explanation: Independent assortment of chromosomes and crossing over during prophase I create genetic variation.

text: How many turns of the light independent reaction cycle are required to make one molecule of triose phosphate?
explanation: Three turns of the Calvin cycle are needed to produce one triose phosphate (3CO₂ → 1 TP).

text: If a student concluded a newly discovered mammal Q feeds its young on milk based on the fact that 'Mammals feed their young on milk'. This is an example of
explanation: This is an example of deductive reasoning.

text: When in the Benedict test reducing sugar (glucose or fructose) and heated copper ion (Cu2+) of copper sulfate (CuSO4) is reduced to a______ of cuprous oxide (Cu+) is formed.
explanation: A red precipitate indicates the presence of reducing sugars in the Benedict test.

text: Which one of the following is not the characteristics of Basidiomycetes?
options: They have fruiting structure known as basidiocap or basidioma
They have a sexual spore known as basidiospore
They produce clamp connection in certain types of hyphae
explanation: Basidiomycetes typically have septate hyphae, not coenocytic.

text: The anterior and posterior body region of insects are called ______________ and ______________, respectively.
explanation: In insects, the anterior region is the head and the posterior region is the abdomen, with the thorax in between.

text: The first step in scientific research is
explanation: Defining the problem is the first step in scientific research.

text: Lampreys belong to the group:
explanation: Lampreys are classified under Agnatha, which are jawless fish.

text: On the basis of their origin, natural resources are categorized as:
explanation: Natural resources are commonly categorized into renewable and non-renewable.

text: Identify the correct statement regarding Mendel's law of dominance;
options: Every character is coded by a pair of factors
Each sex cell receives one of the factor pairs
One factor of the pair completely masks the effect of the other
The inheritance of one factor is independent of the other(s)
correctAnswer: One factor of the pair completely masks the effect of the other
explanation: Mendel's law of dominance states that when two contrasting alleles for a trait are present, only the dominant allele will be expressed in the phenotype, completely masking the effect of the recessive allele. The other options refer to different principles: the law of segregation (options 1 and 2) and the law of independent assortment (option 4).

text: The word Ecology was first used and describes as 'the scientific study of the interactions between organisms and their environment' by:
explanation: Ernst Haeckel is credited with coining the term ecology.

text: _______ the mode of arrangement of sepals or petals on floral bud
explanation: Aestivation refers to the arrangement of sepals or petals in a floral bud.

text: Which one of the following represents seed plants only?
explanation: Spermatophyte refers specifically to seed plants.

text: Which one of the following is not true about ascomycetes?
options: They produce both asexual and sexual reproductive stages
They produce a sac-like structure known as ascus containing ascospores
They don't have a conidial and teleomorphic states
correctAnswer: They don't have a conidial and teleomorphic states
explanation: Ascomycetes do have conidial and teleomorphic states.

text: The effect of different colors of light on the growth of Arabidopsis thaliana (thale cress) seedlings was studied. Three colors of light were tested: blue (450 nm), orange (600 nm), and red (630 nm). Seedling height, shoot length, and biomass were measured in centimeters, centimeters, and grams, respectively. Under blue light, the recorded measurements were 3.5, 2.8, and 2.4. Under orange light, the recorded measurements were 2.3, 2.0, and 2.8. Under red light, the recorded measurements were 7.4, 6.1, and 3.7. What conclusions can be drawn from the data?
options: White light gives the optimal conditions for photosynthesis.
There is a linear relationship between wavelength of light and plant growth.
There is no correlation between total biomass and plant height.
explanation: The data indicates that red light enhances plant growth.

text: To evaluate a proposal, people may likely read ----- of the proposal instead of reading the whole proposal.
explanation: The abstract provides a summary of the proposal.

text: Which of the following statement is incorrect?
options: Virtual population analysis estimates the abundance of population in water
Virtual population analysis enables the scientist to predict the future catches
Harvesting a fish population with compromising its future yields is called sustainable yield
Habitat quality changes affects the population fishes
correctAnswer: Harvesting a fish population with compromising its future yields is called sustainable yield
explanation: The incorrect statement is 'Harvesting a fish population with compromising its future yields is called sustainable yield.' This is wrong because sustainable yield involves harvesting WITHOUT compromising future yields - the statement as written contradicts the definition of sustainability.

text: In the life cycle of the flowering plant which one represented by diploid (2n)?
explanation: The sporophyte is the diploid stage in the life cycle of flowering plants.

text: Which of the following is true?
options: In DNA molecule, the strands are made of H-bonds between complementary bases
DNA is a double stranded molecule
RNA replicates itself in a similar way as DNA
correctAnswer: DNA is a double stranded molecule
explanation: DNA is indeed a double-stranded molecule.

text: Gross Anatomy study about:
explanation: Gross anatomy is the study of anatomical structures that can be observed with the naked eye, without the use of a microscope. It focuses on larger structures rather than microscopic ones, and is not limited to 'large or bloated organs' but includes all macroscopic structures.

text: In genetic maternal effect;
options: Phenotype of the offspring is determined by the genotype of the mother
Phenotype of the mother determines genotypes of the offspring
Inheritance of associated genes is exclusively maternal
Extent of phenotypic expression depends on the genotype of source parents
correctAnswer: Phenotype of the offspring is determined by the genotype of the mother
explanation: In genetic maternal effect, the mother's genotype influences the phenotype of her offspring.

text: Choose the correct answer and encircle on it. Insects are:
options: Arthropods with three pairs of legs
explanation: All statements correctly describe insects.

text: If the order of bases after transcription reads AAGCUGUUAC, what would be the sequence on the sense strand of the parental transcribed DNA molecule?
explanation: If the mRNA sequence is AAGCUGUUAC, then the template DNA strand would be TTCGACAATG (with T instead of U). The sense strand is complementary to the template strand, so it would be AAGCTGTTAC (matching the mRNA but with T instead of U).

text: The culture media that is characterized by its ample agar content is_____
explanation: Solid culture media contain a significant amount of agar.

text: Among the following statements only one is correct, which one is it?
options: In Ethiopia, most fish product is collected from Marine water
The aquaculture in Ethiopia is highly advanced and it is a source of export of the country
Peciforms, Cypriniformes and Siluriformes are most common commercial fishes in Ethiopia
Salmon, Tuna and Cod are common commercial fishes in Ethiopia
correctAnswer: Peciforms, Cypriniformes and Siluriformes are most common commercial fishes in Ethiopia
explanation: Peciforms, Cypriniformes, and Siluriformes are indeed common in Ethiopian waters.

text: Which one of the following is a useful insect?
explanation: Silk-worms are useful for silk production.

text: Among the following which types of resource is matched correctly with its example?
options: Renewable resource = Fossil fuel, Natural gas and Coal
Abiotic resource = Vegetation, Fish population and Birds
Renewable resource = Sunlight, Air and Water
Biotic resource = Soil, Water, Minerals and Air
correctAnswer: Renewable resource = Sunlight, Air and Water
explanation: Sunlight, air, and water are examples of renewable resources.

text: In a dihybrid self-crossing of a plant with genotype DdCc, 3600 offspring were produced. How many of the offspring will have the ddcc genotype?
explanation: In a dihybrid cross, the expected ratio for ddcc is 1/16, so 3600/16 = 225.

text: What is the central role of tRNA in translation?
options: Carrying genetic information from DNA in the nucleus to ribosomes
Recognizing the codon of mRNA and bring the correct amino acid to the ribosomes
Acting as a template for converting a genetic code into amino acid sequence
Assembling the amino acid into a polypeptide chain
correctAnswer: Recognizing the codon of mRNA and bring the correct amino acid to the ribosomes
explanation: tRNA matches mRNA codons with the corresponding amino acids.

text: Which one of the following sentences explains the traditional use of biotechnology?
options: Production of insulin using transgenic bacteria
Production of dairy products at household level
Production of myco-proteins under a laboratory
Production of vinegar using industrial fermenter
correctAnswer: Production of dairy products at household level
explanation: Traditional biotechnology includes domestic food production like dairy processing.

text: A colour blind daughter can be born when the
options: mother is colour blind and the father is normal.
father is colour blind and the mother is normal.
mother is carrier and the father is colour blind.
father is normal and the mother is carrier.
correctAnswer: mother is carrier and the father is colour blind.
explanation: Color blindness is typically X-linked recessive. For a daughter to be colorblind, she must inherit affected X chromosomes from both parents - either an affected X from her father (who must be colorblind) and either a carrier or affected X from her mother. A normal father cannot pass the condition to his daughter.

text: Which of the following animals is not a vertebrate?
explanation: Sea squirts are not vertebrates; they are tunicates.

text: If a child with blood type 'AB' is born from a type 'A' mother and type 'B' father, what would be the possible genotype(s) of the father?
explanation: For a child to have AB blood type, they must receive an A allele from one parent and a B allele from the other. Since the mother is type A, she contributed the A allele. Therefore, the father must have contributed the B allele. The father is type B, so his genotype could be either BB or BO (where O is recessive to both A and B). Since the options only include BO (and not BB), BO is the correct answer.

text: Which of the following feature/s is/are distinguish insects from other classes of Arthropods?
options: Their body divided into three regions (head - thorax - abdomen)
They have three pairs of legs
For most of them, the only arthropods with wings
explanation: Insects are distinguished from other arthropods by a combination of features: (1) their body is divided into three distinct regions - head, thorax, and abdomen; (2) they possess exactly three pairs of jointed legs attached to the thorax; and (3) most insects have wings, which is a feature unique to insects among arthropods. Together, these characteristics form the defining traits of the class Insecta.

text: Which one of the following is correct the composition and level of Genetic diversity from the bottom to top?
explanation: The correct hierarchical order of genetic diversity from bottom (smallest unit) to top (largest) is: Nucleotides --> Genes --> Chromosomes --> Individuals --> Populations. Nucleotides are the basic building blocks of DNA, which form genes, which are organized into chromosomes, which determine the genetic makeup of individuals, which collectively form populations.

text: Which one of the following is not instinctive behavior?
options: Swimming with dolphins and aquatic animals
Opening mouth in chicks when their mother returns to the nest.
Honeybees dance when they return to the hive after finding a source of food
Blinking when something gets too close to your eye
correctAnswer: Swimming with dolphins and aquatic animals
explanation: Swimming with dolphins is a learned behavior, not instinctive. The other options are examples of instinctive behaviors: chick begging behavior, honeybee dance language, and protective eye reflexes are all innate behaviors that don't require learning.

text: Which one of the following is correct about DNA? It is
options: smaller molecule and coding for only protein.
made of phosphate, sugar and bases.
correctAnswer: made of phosphate, sugar and bases.
explanation: DNA consists of phosphate groups, deoxyribose sugar, and nitrogenous bases.

text: Which one of the following phyla is characterized by a flexible cartilaginous rod-like structure, that runs along the dorsal side of the body?
explanation: Chordates are characterized by the notochord.

text: All of the following are examples of innate behaviours EXCEPT
options: training killer whales at marine parks.
producing tears when dust gets into the eyes.
a fly moving its maggot into more humid environment.
correctAnswer: training killer whales at marine parks.
explanation: Animal training requires learned behavior modification.

text: Which one of the following is an example of territorial behaviour of animals?
options: A male robin threatening an intruder
Fixed action of zebra fish to find a mate
Penguins huddling to reduce heat loss
correctAnswer: A male robin threatening an intruder
explanation: Territoriality involves defending space against intruders.

text: One of the following renowned Ethiopian biologists has developed a vaccine for the rinderpest disease.
explanation: Dr. Tilahun Yilma developed the rinderpest vaccine.

text: Sickle cell anemia is caused by the replacement of glutamic acid by valine at a specific position in the beta chains of hemoglobin. This change is an example of which mutation?
explanation: Amino acid substitution causes sickle cell disease.

text: Stanley Miller conducted spark-discharge experiment by taking a mixture of gases that he thought to represent the primitive atmosphere of the Earth. All of the following were found in his gas mixture EXCEPT
explanation: Miller's experiment used reducing atmosphere without CO₂.

text: During image formation, light is refracted twice before it is focused on the retina. This phenomenon happens at the
explanation: Light is primarily refracted at the cornea (first) and lens (second) before focusing on the retina.

text: Which of the following diseases is caused by a DNA virus?
explanation: Cold sores are caused by herpes simplex virus (HSV), a double-stranded DNA virus. AIDS is caused by HIV (an RNA retrovirus), swine flu by influenza virus (RNA), and coronaviruses (including SARS-CoV-2) are RNA viruses.

text: Which one of the following plants is NOT endemic to Ethiopia?
explanation: Mango is not endemic to Ethiopia, while the others are native Ethiopian plants.

text: Bushing of a plant results from
options: cancellation of the positive effect of apical dominance.
removal of the inhibitory effect of auxin.
decreased production of auxin by side shoots.
increased production of auxin by the main shoot.
correctAnswer: removal of the inhibitory effect of auxin.
explanation: Bushing occurs when apical dominance is removed, allowing lateral buds to grow due to reduced auxin inhibition.

text: Currently, natural resources are being depleted at increasing rate and waste materials are accumulated and discharged freely into water bodies. What is the best strategy to overcome these problems?
explanation: Recycling conserves resources and reduces waste accumulation in the environment.

text: What are the common plants of the boreal forest?
explanation: Boreal forests are dominated by coniferous trees adapted to cold climates.

text: Which one of the following sentences is true about viruses?
options: AIDS is caused by a DNA virus.
Corona virus is a DNA virus.
Swine flu is caused by an RNA virus.
Herpes simplex is a DNA virus.
correctAnswer: Herpes simplex is a DNA virus.
explanation: Herpes simplex virus is a DNA virus, while HIV (AIDS), coronaviruses, and influenza (swine flu) are RNA viruses.

text: Why are arctic animals such as seals, walruses and whales large in body size? To
options: move in the water bodies easily
explanation: Large body size reduces surface area to volume ratio, minimizing heat loss in cold environments (Bergmann's rule).

text: When three fatty acid molecules and a glycerol molecule combine in a condensation reaction, they form
explanation: Fatty acids join glycerol via ester bonds to form triglycerides.

text: Assume you are trying to demonstrate breathing movements using artificial lung and you pulled down the rubber sheet. This action of pulling represents which step of the actual breathing process?
options: Exhalation and contraction of the diaphragm
Inhalation and relaxation of the diaphragm
Inhalation and contraction of the diaphragm
Exhalation and relaxation of the diaphragm
correctAnswer: Inhalation and contraction of the diaphragm
explanation: Pulling down the rubber sheet simulates diaphragm contraction during inhalation.

text: Niacin is used to make the coenzyme
explanation: Niacin (vitamin B3) is a precursor for NAD (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide).

text: Assume you wanted to demonstrate a simple reflex action using the knee jerk reflex. You asked a friend to sit with one leg crossed over the other. Which one of the following indicates the correct demonstration?
options: Pulling down your friend's leg that is followed by downward movement
Hitting your friend on the toes followed by sudden upward movement of the leg
Bending up your friend's leg followed by downward movement of the leg
Hitting your friend below the knee cap followed by a sudden upward movement
correctAnswer: Hitting your friend below the knee cap followed by a sudden upward movement
explanation: The patellar reflex is tested by tapping the patellar tendon below the kneecap, causing leg extension.

text: During DNA replication
options: DNA helicase transports nucleotides that are used to build the new DNA.
the base sequence in the new DNA will be slightly changed from the parent DNA.
DNA polymerase assembles new nucleotides into a new strand.
the parent DNA will become different from the daughter DNA.
correctAnswer: DNA polymerase assembles new nucleotides into a new strand.
explanation: DNA polymerase adds complementary nucleotides to synthesize new DNA strands during replication.

text: From the following options, which one contains the steps of writing a scientific report in the correct order?
options: Title → Prediction → Hypothesis → Procedure → Evaluation → Conclusion → Results → Acknowledgement
Title → Hypothesis → Prediction → Procedure → Results → Conclusion → Evaluation → Acknowledgement
Title → Hypothesis → Prediction → Evaluation → Results → Procedure → Conclusion → Acknowledgement
Title → Hypothesis → Procedure → Prediction → Results → Conclusion → Evaluation → Acknowledgement
correctAnswer: Title → Hypothesis → Prediction → Procedure → Results → Conclusion → Evaluation → Acknowledgement
explanation: The standard scientific report order is: Title, Introduction (Hypothesis/Prediction), Methods, Results, Conclusion, Evaluation, Acknowledgement.

text: A review article is written by reading
options: original articles on the same topic
analyzing primary data or secondary data
