text: Which one is correct about the Ethiopian Woodland Savanna vegetation?
options: It is very similar to European Alpine vegetation.
It is known for dense acacia trees.
It grows mainly along the river banks.
It is found both in the highlands and lowlands.
correctAnswer: It is known for dense acacia trees.
explanation: The Ethiopian Woodland Savanna is characterized by dense acacia trees.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: Which one of the following explains the temporal variation of rainfall in Ethiopia?
options: Spring is the rainy season in most parts of Ethiopia.
In Autumn, many places in Ethiopia receive the highest rainfall.
There is little seasonal variation in the amount of rain in Ethiopia.
The lowlands of Afar typically receive rain in summer.
correctAnswer: In Autumn, many places in Ethiopia receive the highest rainfall.
explanation: Autumn (Kiremt season) is when most parts of Ethiopia receive their highest rainfall.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: What characterizes the inland drainage system of Ethiopia?
options: It drains most parts of the northwestern Ethiopia.
It includes the river basins of the Ono-Ghibe.
Its rivers join the Red sea during the summer season.
It is the largest in terms of the discharge of water.
correctAnswer: It includes the river basins of the Ono-Ghibe.
explanation: The inland drainage system of Ethiopia includes river basins like the Ono-Ghibe (Omo-Gibe) that flow into lakes or depressions rather than reaching the sea. These rivers terminate within the land mass, often in the Rift Valley lakes.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: Which of the following is the southern limit of the Western lowlands?
explanation: The Baro-Akobo lowlands form the southern limit of the Western lowlands in Ethiopia.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: Which one describes the general characteristics of Ethiopian rivers?
options: They are very suitable for water transportation.
Most rivers originate from lowland areas.
They are perennial with steady volume of water.
They serve as domestic and international boundaries.
correctAnswer: They serve as domestic and international boundaries.
explanation: Many Ethiopian rivers serve as important domestic and international boundaries.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: Why was hilltops mainly preferred for the establishment of old urban centers of Ethiopia? This was due to their
explanation: Hilltops provided defensive advantages for Ethiopia's old urban centers.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: Among the most common woods of Ethiopia, which one has been traditionally used for making water pipes and baskets?
explanation: Bamboo has been traditionally used for making water pipes and baskets in Ethiopia.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: How do you analyze the hydro politics of the Nile River?
options: Lower course countries are the least beneficiary of the River water.
The Great Ethiopian Renaissance Dam will benefit the neighboring countries.
White Nile is the largest supplier of water to the Nile River.
Historically, Nile basin countries have been fairly utilizing the River water.
correctAnswer: The Great Ethiopian Renaissance Dam will benefit the neighboring countries.
explanation: The GERD is designed to provide benefits to neighboring countries through regulated water flow, reduced flooding, siltation control, and potential electricity exports, while also addressing Ethiopia's domestic energy needs.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: What is the main environmental policy focus area of the Ethiopian green legacy program?
options: Policy related to soil and agriculture
Policy allied to forest, woodland and tree resources
correctAnswer: Policy allied to forest, woodland and tree resources
explanation: The Green Legacy program primarily focuses on forest, woodland and tree resources.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: As a citizen of Ethiopia, what is your view about the advantage your country gained as a result of globalization?
options: It marks the domination of imported products.
It increases the flow of remittance.
It helps to exercise the western cultures.
It encourages a high consumption of domestic products.
correctAnswer: It increases the flow of remittance.
explanation: Increased remittances from Ethiopians abroad is a significant benefit of globalization.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: What should policy makers in Ethiopia do to boost the economy?
options: Encouraging state control of the economy
Encouraging population growth of the country
explanation: Export diversification would strengthen Ethiopia's economy.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: Why was the Plan for Accelerated and Sustained Development to End Poverty (PASDEP) not successful as planned in Ethiopia?
options: Because of a lack of study support from experts
Due to the then global financial crisis
Because of the recurrent flooding in the country
Due to shortage of working labor force
correctAnswer: Due to the then global financial crisis
explanation: The 2008 global financial crisis significantly impacted PASDEP's implementation.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: How do you describe the economic growth and development trend of Ethiopia?
options: Many settlements have access to all-weather roads.
The country has the highest literacy rates in Africa.
Malnutrition is a serious problem in urban areas than it is in rural areas.
School dropouts are higher in urban areas than are in rural areas.
correctAnswer: Many settlements have access to all-weather roads.
explanation: Improved road infrastructure has been a notable development in Ethiopia.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: How is the relative location of the Horn of Africa described?
options: It is adjoined by the Red Sea in the northeast.
It is bounded in the northwest by the Indian Ocean.
It is situated to the southeast of Asia.
It is bordered by the Sudan in the southwest.
correctAnswer: It is adjoined by the Red Sea in the northeast.
explanation: The Horn is bordered by the Red Sea to the northeast.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: Which one of the following has widely been practiced as a climate change adaptation strategy in Ethiopia?
explanation: Tree plantation has been widely practiced in Ethiopia as a climate change adaptation strategy.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: What is the main characteristic of indigenous conflict resolution practices in Ethiopia?
options: It passes lengthy processes to bring about reconciliation.
The issue is concluded in reconciliation and harmony.
Most of them are mainly based on written laws.
correctAnswer: The issue is concluded in reconciliation and harmony.
explanation: Indigenous conflict resolution in Ethiopia typically concludes with reconciliation and harmony.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: Among the following zones of Ethiopia, which one is densely populated?
explanation: Gedeo zone is among Ethiopia's most densely populated areas.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: Which one explains about the lowlands of Ethiopia?
options: Kobar sink is the lowest place in the country.
Tekeze occupies the floor of the rift valley.
Lowlands are situated at the center of the country.
They are found in between 1000-2000 m heights.
correctAnswer: Kobar sink is the lowest place in the country.
explanation: Kobar sink is Ethiopia's lowest point.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: In which geological Era is the rift valley of Ethiopia formed?
explanation: Ethiopia's Rift Valley formed in the Cenozoic.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: Which one of the following relates to the economic policies of Ethiopia?
options: Emphasizing on an economic system fully controlled by the state
Focusing on shifting urban labor force to rural-based economy
Promoting regional administration in economic management
correctAnswer: Promoting regional administration in economic management
explanation: Ethiopia promotes regional economic management.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: Which part of Ethiopia is in high drought probability zone?
explanation: Afar region experiences frequent droughts.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: Where is the highest mean annual temperature recorded?
explanation: Dallol has Ethiopia's highest temperatures.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: Which specific pillar of Ethiopia’s Climate-Resilient Green Economy (CRGE) strategy focuses on advancing the use of renewable energy sources?
explanation: Pillar III focuses on advancing the use of renewable energy sources.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: Which of the following is NOT a commonly identified adaptation strategy in Ethiopia?
explanation: Reducing fossil fuel use is not a commonly identified adaptation strategy in Ethiopia.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: Which strategy is part of Ethiopia’s Climate Change Resilient Green-Economy (CRGES)?
explanation: Promoting agro-forestry is a strategy aimed at enhancing resilience to climate change.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: Why are developing nations like Ethiopia more vulnerable to climate change impacts?
options: Higher per capita greenhouse gas emissions
Limited financial and technological resources for adaptation
correctAnswer: Limited financial and technological resources for adaptation
explanation: Developing nations often lack the resources needed to effectively adapt to climate change.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: Which Ethiopian ethnic group uses the T’eer as an indigenous conflict resolution system?
explanation: The Oromo ethnic group uses the T’eer system for conflict resolution.

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: Assess which traditional agro-climatic zone of Ethiopia is most represented by the map area?
explanation: The elevation range (200-300m) suggests Dega zone (temperate highland climate).

topicName: Geography of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa
text: Which traditional agro-climatic zone in Ethiopia is most recognized for producing surplus grains to support food security?
explanation: Woina dega (mid-altitude) is Ethiopia's primary grain-producing zone.

text: The type of survey that involves continuous recording of events like births, deaths, marriages, and divorces refers to:
explanation: Vital registration is the continuous and systematic recording of vital events such as births, deaths, marriages, and divorces. Census surveys, in contrast, are conducted periodically to collect comprehensive population data.

text: Country A has an area of 80,000 km² and a population size of 4,000,000 with 20% urban population. Country B has an area of 10,000 km² and a population size of 2,000,000 with 80% urban population. Which of the following is correct about the crude density of country A and B?
options: Population of country A is dense in comparison to country B
Population of country A is sparse in comparison to country B
correctAnswer: Population of country A is sparse in comparison to country B
explanation: The crude density for country A is 4,000,000/80,000 = 50P/km², while for country B it is 2,000,000/10,000 = 200P/km². Therefore, country A's population is sparse compared to country B's population.

text: In Ethiopia, when is a given settlement considered as an urban settlement?
options: When the residents depend on different economic activities
When houses are made up of simple construction materials
When the inhabitants are primarily engaged in agriculture
When population size exceeds one thousand people
correctAnswer: When the residents depend on different economic activities
explanation: Diverse economic activities define urban settlements in Ethiopia.

text: What is the major factor that makes the Nile valley of Egypt one of the most densely populated areas of the world?
explanation: Fertile Nile soils support intensive agriculture and dense populations.

text: What could be generalized about the population structure of Ethiopia?
options: In urban areas, the size of male population is greater than that of the female population.
One-fourth of the total population of Ethiopia is the elderly population.
In most rural areas, the number of males is greater than that of females.
Ethiopia has the smallest size of economically active population.
correctAnswer: In most rural areas, the number of males is greater than that of females.
explanation: Rural Ethiopia typically has more males than females.

text: Which one of the following is true about Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per capita?
options: It measures a country's economic output per person
It shows how much economic production value can be attributed to each individual citizen
It helps to understand how the economy is growing with its population
explanation: All statements about GDP per capita are true.

text: What does the Gini coefficient of '1 (or 100%)' indicate in terms of income distribution among the population of a country?
options: One person receives all the national income
Income is perfectly split between all members of society
correctAnswer: One person receives all the national income
explanation: A Gini coefficient of 1 (or 100%) represents perfect inequality, meaning one person has all the income and everyone else has none. Conversely, a Gini coefficient of 0 represents perfect equality where income is distributed equally among all members of society.

text: Which of the following world population node is inhabited by about 60% of world population?
explanation: The Asiatic population belt is home to a significant portion of the world's population.

text: Which one of the following is the main reason for the high rate of deforestation in Africa?
options: The increased need for fuel wood
explanation: All listed reasons contribute to the high rate of deforestation in Africa.

text: Country A has an area of 80,000 km² and a population size of 4,000,000 with 20% urban population. Country B has an area of 10,000 km² and a population size of 2,000,000 with 80% urban population. Which one of the following is correct regarding the settlement of country A and B?
options: Level of urbanization is high for country B in comparison to country A
Level of urbanization is high for country A in comparison to country B
Both country A and B are rural settlements
correctAnswer: Level of urbanization is high for country B in comparison to country A
explanation: The level of urbanization for country B (80% of population is urban) is higher than country A (only 20% urban). This means country B has a much higher proportion of its population living in urban areas compared to country A, despite having a smaller total population.

text: ______________ refers to the total value of goods and services produced in a country over a period of time.
explanation: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) measures the total value of goods and services produced.

text: The Ethiopian industrial sector is characterized by the following features EXCEPT:
explanation: The Ethiopian industrial sector is characterized by light industries and small-scale manufacturing rather than high (heavy) industries. The sector faces challenges including capital scarcity, shortage of skilled labor, and low production levels.

text: Which one of the following IS NOT a serious factor of socioeconomic development in Ethiopia?
options: Insignificant decline in the rate of population growth
correctAnswer: Insignificant decline in the rate of population growth
explanation: An insignificant decline in population growth is not a serious factor affecting development.

text: Which one of the following IS NOT TRUE about the population policy of Ethiopia?
options: Ethiopia adopted the anti-natalist population policy
It aimed at widening the gap between high population growth and low economic productivity
Its general objective is ensuring environmental protections
It aimed at reducing the rate of rural-to-urban migration
correctAnswer: It aimed at widening the gap between high population growth and low economic productivity
explanation: The policy does not aim to widen the gap between population growth and productivity.

text: A form of agriculture in Ethiopia in which farmers practice the rearing of livestock side by side with crop production is ___________.
explanation: Mixed farming involves both livestock rearing and crop production.

text: Which one of the following is the characteristics of developing countries?
explanation: Developing countries typically have low per capita incomes. Other common characteristics (not listed in the options) include high population growth rates, dependence on primary sector, lower literacy rates, higher incidence of diseases, and less mechanized farming.

text: In the 2007 national census, the sex ratio of the Ethiopian population was 100.8. What does it refer?
options: Males and females are exactly equal in number
explanation: A sex ratio of 100.8 indicates that males slightly outnumber females.

text: Which one of the following IS TRUE about assumptions of Malthusian population theory?
options: Passion between sexes is inevitable and universal
Food production is limited, and population cannot increase beyond the means of subsistence
If population growth outstrips the means of subsistence, 'positive checks' will apply
explanation: All statements reflect assumptions of Malthusian population theory.

text: Country A has an area of 80,000 km² and a population size of 4,000,000 with 20% urban population. Country B has an area of 10,000 km² and a population size of 2,000,000 with 80% urban population. What is the rural density of country B?
explanation: Rural population of country B = Total population × (1 - Urban population percentage) = 2,000,000 × (1 - 0.8) = 2,000,000 × 0.2 = 400,000. Rural density = Rural population ÷ Area = 400,000 ÷ 10,000 = 40P/km². Therefore the correct answer is 40P/km².

text: Which one of the following economic activities is tertiary economic activity?
explanation: Communication is a tertiary economic activity, which involves providing services rather than producing goods. Tertiary activities include transportation, communication, banking, education, healthcare, etc. Agricultural production is primary, mining is primary, and research is typically classified as quaternary.

text: Which one of the following is true about the significance of population studies?
options: It is helpful for socio-economic development planning
It is helpful to estimate labor force for the productive economic sectors
It is helpful to estimate the creator of material wealth
explanation: Population studies are significant for various aspects of socio-economic planning.

text: Which one of the following components of population change is non-biological?
explanation: Migration is a non-biological component of population change.

text: Which one of the following is a non-renewable natural resource?
explanation: Minerals are considered non-renewable natural resources.

text: Which one of the following is a conservation method used in Ethiopia to protect wildlife?
options: Educating the public about environment protection
explanation: All listed methods are used for wildlife conservation in Ethiopia.

text: Which of the following is the most appropriate practice of water conservation?
explanation: Check dams are effective for water conservation.

text: What is the importance of identifying and applying appropriate sampling techniques?
options: To increase bias in the results
To ensure a larger sample size
explanation: Appropriate sampling techniques ensure accurate results.

text: Settlement morphology, a key focus in cultural geography, refers to:
options: The physical layout and architectural form of human settlements, reflect historical, cultural, and environmental influences, shaping urban landscapes.
The genetic composition and demographic characteristics of urban populations encompass diversity, migration patterns, and social stratification.
The socioeconomic structures and dynamics of rural communities, elucidating livelihood strategies, land tenure systems, and resource management practices.
The linguistic diversity and cultural heterogeneity within urban neighborhoods exemplify the coexistence and interaction of various ethnic and social groups.
correctAnswer: The physical layout and architectural form of human settlements, reflect historical, cultural, and environmental influences, shaping urban landscapes.
explanation: Settlement morphology focuses on the physical layout and architectural form of settlements.

text: Which of the following is a method of data collection?
explanation: Conducting experiments is a primary method of data collection. While reviewing literature is important for research, it involves gathering existing data rather than collecting new data.

text: Population pyramid is:
options: Graphic representation of age and sex structure of population
It does not show age and sex structure
correctAnswer: Graphic representation of age and sex structure of population
explanation: A population pyramid graphically represents the age and sex structure of a population.

text: What is the significance of understanding the relationship between terrain and form in geomorphology?
options: It helps in predicting weather patterns.
It aids in urban planning and development.
It is crucial for environmental conservation efforts.
explanation: Understanding terrain and form is essential for various applications including weather prediction, urban planning, and conservation.

text: Which one of the following IS NOT characteristic of population census?
explanation: All listed options are characteristics of a population census.

text: Which one of the following IS NOT true about natural resources?
options: They are often characterized by the amount of biodiversity that exists in various ecosystems
They are derived from the environment
They include automobiles, phones, computers, etc.
correctAnswer: They include automobiles, phones, computers, etc.
explanation: Natural resources do not include manufactured goods like automobiles and computers.

text: If you are asked to propose a strategy for conservation of wildlife where hunting is strictly forbidden, what would be your suggestion as conservation area?
explanation: Sanctuaries are areas where hunting is strictly prohibited for wildlife conservation.

text: How do the relative compact shape and unbroken coastline of Africa impact its development?
options: Its compact shape discourages intra-continental movements.
Its unbroken coastline makes the continent rich in natural harbors.
Its unbroken coastline encourages external communications.
Its compact shape relatively eases administration and defense.
correctAnswer: Its compact shape discourages intra-continental movements.
explanation: Africa's relatively compact shape with few indentations and unbroken coastline limits natural harbors and intra-continental movement, which has historically hindered trade and contributed to development challenges.

text: Despite many efforts, wild life resources of Africa are deteriorating from time to time. If you are asked to prioritize and implement conservation measures, which one is the most important one?
options: Establishing national parks and game reserves
Regulating the practice of illegal hunting
explanation: Community awareness is foundational to sustainable wildlife conservation.

text: How do you describe the population size and growth of Africa?
options: It has the lowest rate of population growth rate.
Its population doubling time is the longest.
It is the least populated continent.
It has a negative net migration rate.
correctAnswer: It has the lowest rate of population growth rate.
explanation: Africa has the highest rate of population growth and the shortest population doubling time among all continents, not the lowest. This answer is incorrectly marked and should be the opposite of what's stated.

text: Which of the following is a major cause of deforestation?
explanation: Urbanization, agricultural expansion, and logging are all major causes of deforestation.

text: What makes the regions of Africa similar from the socio-economic and geopolitical points of view?
options: There is a strong political integration among the regions.
In each region, about two-thirds of the population lives in urban areas.
Each region has direct access to the sea.
They depend mainly on mechanized agriculture.
correctAnswer: There is a strong political integration among the regions.
explanation: Despite their diversity, African regions have been working toward political integration through organizations like the African Union, which creates similarities in their socio-economic and geopolitical structures. This integration affects trade policies, diplomatic relations, and regional development strategies.

text: What is the effect of advancement in transport and communication on the location of economic activities?
options: It shows how distance and time impact on the production of goods.
It enforces the establishment of industries where raw materials found.
It enables delivery and sale of perishable goods at a reasonable time.
It encourages people to deliver their goods and services in person.
correctAnswer: It enables delivery and sale of perishable goods at a reasonable time.
explanation: Improved transport allows perishable goods distribution.

text: Which statement relates to theories on population growth and development?
options: Marxians believe that population growth causes technological development.
Ester Boserup believes that there is a strong linkage between poverty and population growth.
Neo-Malthusianism asserts that socio-economic problems are solved by reducing birth rate.
Malthusian theory stresses that food production exceeds population growth.
correctAnswer: Neo-Malthusianism asserts that socio-economic problems are solved by reducing birth rate.
explanation: Neo-Malthusians advocate birth control for development.

text: Trade imbalance occurs in developing countries when
options: a country has industries owned by foreigners.
a country borrows money to import goods for its population.
the value of goods of a country's export is higher than its import.
the amount of import item is less than that of export item.
correctAnswer: a country borrows money to import goods for its population.
explanation: Trade imbalance (specifically a trade deficit) occurs when a country imports more than it exports in value terms. This is particularly problematic for developing countries when they borrow money to finance imports, creating both trade and fiscal deficits that can lead to economic instability and dependency.

text: What is the dominant factor responsible for the current depleting African elephant population?
explanation: Poaching for ivory has been the primary factor in the dramatic decline of African elephant populations. While habitat loss and fragmentation (including deforestation) also contribute significantly, the illegal ivory trade driven by demand in Asia has caused the most severe and rapid population declines.

text: In which parts of Ethiopia do you mostly observe permanent rural settlements?
explanation: Permanent rural settlements are most common in crop farming areas where agriculture is stable.

text: In which one of the following continents is the population doubling time very short?
explanation: Asia has rapid population growth with short doubling times.

text: What kind of measures do you recommend for water resource management and conservation in Ethiopia?
options: Building dams to generate hydroelectric power
Planting exotic plants near the streams and rivers
Planting trees on the upper parts of the streams
Rain water harvesting in the wettest parts of the country
correctAnswer: Planting trees on the upper parts of the streams
explanation: Planting trees on the upper parts of streams helps with water conservation by reducing erosion and maintaining water flow.

text: Which of the population theories below considers the loss of human life through drought as a positive check to control fast population growth?
explanation: Neo-Malthusian theory views natural disasters like drought as positive checks on population growth.

text: What is the soil conservation measure that involves resting of arable land for a limited period of time called?
explanation: Fallowing is the practice of leaving land uncultivated to restore its fertility.

text: Which one of the following explains the trend of population growth rate of Ethiopia?
options: Currently, the rate of population growth shows a slight decline.
Between 1984 and 2007, there was a fast population growth rate.
At present, Ethiopia is the third most populous country in Africa.
Before the 1930, the rate of population growth was very high.
correctAnswer: Currently, the rate of population growth shows a slight decline.
explanation: Recent data shows Ethiopia's population growth rate has been declining slightly.

text: Which of the following actions should be taken first to conserve natural vegetation in Ethiopia?
explanation: Community awareness is fundamental before implementing any conservation measures. Without local understanding and support, other conservation efforts like establishing protected areas or implementing sustainable practices will face resistance and likely fail in the long term.

text: How does Boserup's hypothesis differ from Malthus's theory?
explanation: Boserup argued population growth drives innovation, contrasting Malthus's pessimistic view.

text: Why are some rare animals of Ethiopia approaching extinction? This is due to the
explanation: Habitat loss due to expanding human settlements is the primary threat to Ethiopia's rare animals.

text: What important message do you expect to hear in a speech to be delivered on the population policy of Ethiopia?
options: Establishing youth reproductive health counselling centers
correctAnswer: Establishing youth reproductive health counselling centers
explanation: Ethiopia's population policy emphasizes reproductive health education.

text: In Ethiopian context, which impact of rapid population growth is critical, compared to others?
explanation: Deforestation is the most critical impact due to the need for more agricultural land.

text: In which one of the following countries do you expect very diverse natural resources?
explanation: Ethiopia has the most diverse natural resources among these countries.

text: One of the following conditions can be taken as evidence of a promising future for socioeconomic development in Ethiopia. Which one is it?
explanation: Ethiopia's diverse natural resources provide potential for future development.

text: What is the major factor that forces people to migrate from their places of origin in search of employment?
explanation: Economic needs are the primary driver of labor migration.

text: If you were a member of your school environmental conservation club, which of the following would you advice the community to do?
options: Protecting water bodies from disposal of waste materials
Encouraging extraction of forest resources for furniture purposes
Promoting free grazing of domestic animals in national parks
correctAnswer: Protecting water bodies from disposal of waste materials
explanation: Protecting water bodies is fundamental to environmental conservation.

text: Among the following, which one is an example of a renewable natural resource?
explanation: Soil is a renewable resource when properly managed.

text: How does the World Bank contribute to the economic development of the developing countries?
explanation: World Bank provides funding for large development projects.

text: How has advancement in transport and communication technology brought changes in the location of economic activities?
options: By enabling producers to sell perishable goods fresh anywhere.
By facilitating the location of industries to be close to the source of raw materials.
By increasing the transportation cost of manufactured goods from producers to consumers.
By supporting industrial workers to live close to their work place.
correctAnswer: By enabling producers to sell perishable goods fresh anywhere.
explanation: Improved transport allows perishable goods to reach distant markets.

text: What is the implication of the low level of urbanization in Africa?
options: Low rate of urban to urban migration
Low cost of urban transport facilities
Low living standard of urban population
Low rate of rural to urban migration
correctAnswer: Low rate of rural to urban migration
explanation: Low urbanization reflects limited rural-urban migration.

text: What is the main reason that makes intra-continental trade to be low in Africa?
options: The diverse nature of the economy
correctAnswer: The diverse nature of the economy
explanation: The diverse nature of African economies limits complementary trade within the continent because many countries produce similar primary commodities for export rather than diversified products that could be traded with neighboring countries. This similarity in economic outputs reduces opportunities for mutually beneficial trade exchanges within Africa.

text: In which of the following countries is the contribution of Gold to its economic development the highest in Africa?
explanation: South Africa's economy relies heavily on gold production.

text: Which one of the following is the main reason for the high rate of urbanization in Ethiopia?
options: The presence of a large number of immigrants
The presence of a high rate of natural increase
Urban development policy of the country
correctAnswer: The presence of a high rate of natural increase
explanation: Natural population increase drives Ethiopia's urbanization.

text: What is the Crude Birth Rate of the region?
explanation: CBR = (Live births / Total population) × 1000 = (196,189 / 11,818,619) × 1000 ≈ 16.6 per 1000.

text: What is the rate of natural increase of the population?
explanation: RNI = CBR - CDR = 16.6 - 5.5 = 11.1 per 1000, which equals 1.1% when expressed as a percentage.

text: What does the age dependency ratio of 43% imply?
options: It refers to 100 persons who are dependent on every 43 economically active persons.
It shows 57% of the total population is dependent on 43% of the labor force.
It implies that 43% of the total population is economically active.
It means 43% of the total population depends on economically active labor force.
correctAnswer: It means 43% of the total population depends on economically active labor force.
explanation: Dependency ratio shows the proportion of dependents to working-age population.

text: If you were asked by a tourist who wanted to see Chelada babobu in Ethiopia, which specific national park would be your recommendation?
explanation: The Semen Highlands National Park is known for its Gelada baboon (Chelada babobu) population, which is endemic to the Ethiopian highlands.

text: What type of migration results when governments move war and natural disaster-affected people to new places?
explanation: Resettlement refers to government-organized relocation of affected populations.

text: Which measure of soil conservation should be widely used against soil erosion in arid and semi-arid areas of the Horn?
explanation: Shelter belts (rows of trees) are effective in reducing wind erosion in arid and semi-arid areas.

text: Why are some regions of the world more sparsely populated than others? This is because of the
explanation: Rugged topography makes areas less suitable for settlement and agriculture.

text: How do we generalize the level of the world's urbanization across continents?
options: Africa has the highest level of urbanization.
Asia has a higher level of urbanization than Latin America.
North America is the most urbanized continent.
There is a high level of urbanization in the developing world.
correctAnswer: North America is the most urbanized continent.
explanation: North America has the highest urbanization level among continents.

text: How do we describe rural and urban settlements?
options: Rural areas are known by dense population.
Urban areas have a low division of labor.
explanation: Urban settlements typically feature planned street layouts.

text: Which of the following distinguishes the regions of Africa?
options: Eastern Africa is the smallest in terms of area.
Western Africa has the highest urban population.
Central Africa is the most sparsely populated.
Northern Africa has the highest number of countries.
correctAnswer: Central Africa is the most sparsely populated.
explanation: Central Africa has the lowest population density among African regions.

text: In what ways does the presence of many waterfalls, rapids and steep courses of African rivers tend to mainly benefit the socioeconomic development of the continent?
options: By creating conducive environment for fishing
explanation: Waterfalls and rapids provide excellent sites for hydroelectric power generation.

text: What motivated the government of Ethiopia to develop anti-natalist population policy? The need to
options: reduce the rate of urban-rural migration
balance the number of male and female population
raise the economic and social status of women
correctAnswer: raise the economic and social status of women
explanation: Ethiopia's anti-natalist policies aim to improve women's socioeconomic status through family planning.

text: If you find a large number of herbivore and carnivore animals in a certain geographical area in Africa, what can you generalize about the type of the climate of the area?
explanation: Tropical Savanna climates support diverse herbivore and carnivore populations.

text: Among the following, which one describes the international migration in Africa?
options: Brain drain is bringing more opportunities than challenges.
It has modified the sociocultural assets of North Africa.
Its practice has a short history in the continent.
Currently, there is the highest number of immigrants to the continent.
correctAnswer: It has modified the sociocultural assets of North Africa.
explanation: International migration has significantly influenced North Africa's sociocultural characteristics.

text: What is the main implication of the large size of young population in Ethiopia?
options: The country has the smallest proportion of non-productive population.
The country needs a high expenditure for the provision of basic social services.
It has a low potential to increase the momentum of population growth.
There is a rapid socio-economic and technological development of the country.
correctAnswer: The country needs a high expenditure for the provision of basic social services.
explanation: A large youth population requires substantial investment in education and services.

text: What could be generalized about the economic growth and development trend of Africa?
options: Rapid population growth acts as an engine to many African economies.
Different economic sectors of the continent are being integrated.
Manufactured products dominated the export items of the continent.
Most African countries exhibit a negative trade balance.
correctAnswer: Most African countries exhibit a negative trade balance.
explanation: Many African nations import more than they export, resulting in trade deficits.

text: Let's say your birth place has a rapid rate population growth which pushes the residents of the area to permanently leave their place of living. What do you think might your place of birth benefit from these permanent migrants?
options: It solves the problem of labor shortage
It results in high concentrations of elders
It decreases pressure on natural resources
It increases the rate of population growth
correctAnswer: It decreases pressure on natural resources
explanation: Out-migration can reduce pressure on local resources in rapidly growing areas.

text: Which feature best explains the socioeconomic condition of developed countries?
explanation: High urbanization is a key characteristic of developed nations.

text: How does the International Monetary Fund (IMF) contribute to the economic development of nations?
options: By promoting countries to set tariffs and quotas
By encouraging state ownership of enterprises
explanation: A key IMF function is helping stabilize international exchange rates.

text: What was the central argument of Malthusian Population Theory?
options: Rapid population growth leads to underdevelopment
correctAnswer: Rapid population growth leads to underdevelopment
explanation: Malthus argued that population grows geometrically while food production grows arithmetically, leading to poverty and underdevelopment. He proposed that 'positive checks' (war, famine, disease) and 'preventive checks' (moral restraint) would limit population growth.

text: Which one of the following is the main impact of rapid population growth in Ethiopia?
explanation: Soil degradation from overuse is a major consequence of rapid population growth.

text: How do you explain the settlement pattern of the Ethiopian population?
options: The Shewa and Harerghe plateaus host fewer urban populations.
Many urban areas in Ethiopia lie along major transport routes.
Peripheral areas are mainly associated with permanent settlement.
Most highland areas in northern Ethiopia have temporary settlements.
correctAnswer: Many urban areas in Ethiopia lie along major transport routes.
explanation: Ethiopian urban centers are concentrated along transportation corridors.

text: Among the following, which one is primarily used to gather population data from a segment of the whole population?
explanation: Sample surveys collect data from representative population segments.

text: What change is mainly brought due to the development of transport and communication technologies?
options: Distance and time have got great impact on the production
Production of perishable products near major urban centers
Location of industries near resources and energy supplies
Working for companies without physically being there
correctAnswer: Working for companies without physically being there
explanation: Advanced communications enable remote work arrangements.

text: Which of the following country is the leading in fish processing industry in Africa?
explanation: Morocco has Africa's most developed fish processing sector.

text: Which one of the following is the sparsely populated part of the world?
explanation: Northern Canada and Alaska in Northeastern North America have some of the lowest population densities in the world due to harsh climate conditions.

text: What is the main cause of conflict over natural resources such as the River Nile?
explanation: Political factors are the main cause of conflicts over natural resources like the Nile.

text: Which one describes the concept of sustainable development?
options: Prioritizing good governance regardless of economic development
Improving human welfare at the expense of the environment
explanation: Sustainable development involves environmental-friendly socio-economic development.

text: Which one of the following plays a decisive role to govern natural resources sustainably?
options: Prioritizing the participation of males in resource management
Fostering top-down decision making in resource management
Giving exclusive rights to the government in managing resources
explanation: Indigenous resource management systems play a key role in sustainable governance.

text: Which physical factor positively influences the distribution of human population?
options: High relief with very high humidity
High natural increase of human population
explanation: Optimum temperature and rainfall attract human settlement.

text: Which statement refers to the trends of population growth of the world?
options: Population growth has been constantly increasing since 5000BC because of economic diversification.
Rapid population growth was recorded for the first time when humans started to domesticate animals.
Population growth was quite low before 5000BC mainly because of war and use of contraceptives.
The total number of human population was about 4 billion at the beginning of the 1900s.
correctAnswer: Rapid population growth was recorded for the first time when humans started to domesticate animals.
explanation: The first significant acceleration in human population growth coincided with the Neolithic Revolution (around 10,000 BCE) when humans began domesticating animals and practicing agriculture. This transition from hunting-gathering to agriculture created more stable food supplies, allowing for larger, more settled populations.

text: Which one of the following describes the level of urbanization in the world?
options: Europe has the second highest percentage of urban population.
Japan has the highest percentage of urban population.
Developing regions have higher urban population than the world's average.
Africa has higher urban population than other developing regions.
correctAnswer: Europe has the second highest percentage of urban population.
explanation: Europe has the second highest urban population percentage.

text: What will happen by 2030 if the current population growth rate of Ethiopia continues in the same trend?
options: The population will exert pressure on the available infrastructure.
The population will be evenly distributed across the country.
The population density will remain the same.
The size of the population will be quadrupled.
correctAnswer: The population will exert pressure on the available infrastructure.
explanation: Continued growth will strain infrastructure.

text: Which sphere of the earth contains important minerals?
explanation: The lithosphere (Earth's crust and upper mantle) contains the vast majority of Earth's mineral resources. This outer rocky layer is where mining activities extract valuable minerals, metals, and gemstones used in industry and commerce.

text: What is the main task of the World Trade Organization?
options: It directly puts sanctions in a sovereign country when it violates laws.
It practically protects professional workers' rights.
It provides a framework on how to produce exportable items.
It enforces regulations related to free trade agreements.
correctAnswer: It enforces regulations related to free trade agreements.
explanation: WTO enforces free trade agreement regulations.

text: Which environmental movement focuses on preventing human-induced damage to the natural environment?
explanation: Preservation/conservation movements protect nature from human damage.

text: Which of the following is a challenge to environmental sustainability?
explanation: Rapid urbanization strains environmental resources.

text: What is the importance of conducting research on an environmental problem?
options: To investigate causes of the problem
To document the types of problems
correctAnswer: To investigate causes of the problem
explanation: Research helps identify environmental problem causes.

text: Which statement explains the size of the African population?
options: The continent has half of the population of Oceania.
has two-thirds of the world's population.
is more populous than North America.
correctAnswer: is more populous than North America.
explanation: Africa's population exceeds North America's.

text: Which area of the world is sparsely populated mainly due to physical factor?
explanation: Central Africa's harsh climate limits population.

text: Which one of the following describes the sex structure of the African population?
options: In Guinea, the number of female births exceeds that of male births.
In the Sub-Saharan Africa, there are more males than females.
In Uganda, there is a balanced number of males and females.
In the Sub-Saharan Africa, the sex ratio is below the world's mean.
correctAnswer: In the Sub-Saharan Africa, the sex ratio is below the world's mean.
explanation: Sub-Saharan Africa's sex ratio is below global average.

text: Which one describes a population characteristic of southern African as compared to other regions?
explanation: Southern Africa has relatively low immigration.

text: Which statement describes the concept of economic development?
options: Progress in the process of industrial domestic product
Increase in the total amount of manufactured goods
Improvement in the living condition of the people
Increase in the amount of total agricultural production
correctAnswer: Improvement in the living condition of the people
explanation: Economic development improves living standards.

text: Which one of the following is the main disadvantage of migration in the receiving country?
explanation: Ethnic tension is often a significant disadvantage in receiving countries, as large influxes of migrants can lead to social conflicts, competition for resources, housing pressure, and cultural misunderstandings between existing populations and newcomers.

text: What is the effect of rapid population growth on the socio-economic progress of developing countries?
explanation: Rapid growth can cause food insecurity.

text: Which statement is about population growth control practices?
options: Kenya encourages a national family planning policy.
Most African countries have a one-child policy.
China supports women to have large families.
correctAnswer: Kenya encourages a national family planning policy.
explanation: Kenya promotes family planning.

text: Globalization contributes to the economic development of developing countries mainly through
explanation: While the original answer suggested poverty reduction programs, globalization primarily contributes to developing economies through foreign direct investment, technology transfer, access to global markets, and integration into global value chains. Resource extraction is a major aspect, though its benefits to local economies vary greatly depending on governance and economic policies.

text: In which coastal areas of Africa is the tropical maritime climate located?
explanation: The tropical maritime climate is located in the northwestern coastal areas of Africa, particularly along the Gulf of Guinea, where the influence of warm ocean currents and consistent trade winds creates humid conditions year-round.

text: What is the main disadvantage of migration in the receiving country?
explanation: The main disadvantage of migration in receiving countries is often ethnic tension, which can manifest as social conflicts, competition for jobs and public services, cultural misunderstandings, and in some cases, xenophobia or discrimination.

text: What innovative strategy would you propose to strengthen Ethiopia’s resilience to climate change impacts across its diverse regions?
options: Escalation of deforestation and restore forests
explanation: Implementing agroforestry and soil conservation can enhance resilience to climate change.

text: Which of the following is classified as a proximate cause of resource degradation?
explanation: Deforestation is a proximate cause of resource degradation.

text: What does the term 'demographic transition' describe?
options: Shift from high birth/death rates to low
correctAnswer: Shift from high birth/death rates to low
explanation: Demographic transition refers to the shift from high birth and death rates to low rates.

text: Which core pillar of sustainable development emphasizes ensuring equity and fairness in the distribution of resources across populations?
explanation: The social pillar emphasizes equity and fairness in resource distribution.

text: Which of the following pairs of continents have contrasting population situations?
explanation: Africa and North America have contrasting population situations.

text: Which historical theory attributes poverty primarily to excessive reproduction among lower-income populations?
explanation: The Malthusian Theory suggests that excessive reproduction leads to poverty.

text: What measure would you create to effectively control rapid population growth in an overpopulated region?
explanation: Promoting comprehensive sex education is an effective measure to control population growth.

text: What is the key argument of geographical determinism?
explanation: Geographical determinism argues that the environment significantly influences socio-economic development.

text: How does the 1994 Cairo Conference differ from the 1974 World Population Plan?
options: It ties population control to women’s empowerment.
It prioritizes GDP growth over health.
correctAnswer: It ties population control to women’s empowerment.
explanation: The 1994 Cairo Conference emphasized women's empowerment in relation to population control.

text: What is the core argument of Marxist population theory?
options: Poverty stems from unequal resource distribution.
correctAnswer: Poverty stems from unequal resource distribution.
explanation: Marxist theory argues that poverty is a result of unequal distribution of resources.

text: What phase of invasive plant spread involves establishing self-sustaining populations?
explanation: Naturalization is the phase where invasive plants establish self-sustaining populations.

text: According to the Von Thünen’s model, which agricultural product is grown closest to cities?
explanation: Perishable crops are grown closest to cities to minimize transportation time.

text: Which of the following government actions is an example of a direct effect of population policy?
explanation: Raising the age of marriage is a direct effect of population policy aimed at controlling population growth.

text: What type of progression did Thomas Malthus associate with the rapid increase in human population sizes over time?
explanation: Malthus associated population growth with geometric progression.

text: What principle of good natural resource governance aligns with implementing environmental impact assessments?
explanation: Environmental impact assessments promote equitable and sustainable resource use.

text: Among the major global population clusters, which one accounts for the smallest percentage of the world's total population?
explanation: Northeast America has the smallest population among these major clusters.

text: What effect does rapid population growth have on the socio-economic progress of developing countries?
explanation: Rapid growth often outstrips job creation, increasing unemployment.

text: What type of resource scarcity arises when population growth exceeds resource availability?
explanation: Demand-induced scarcity occurs when population growth increases demand beyond supply.

text: What policy would you design to address a country's declining birth rate and increasing elderly population to ensure future stability?
explanation: Pro-natalist policies encourage higher birth rates to counter aging populations.

text: Which one of the following does not refer to Universal Transverse Mercator Coordinate System (UTM)?
options: It is a hybrid coordinate system
The latitudinal extent is from 84° N to 80° S
Each zone has a central meridian called the false easting
explanation: UTM uses a regular grid system, not irregular grids. It divides the Earth into 60 zones, each 6° of longitude wide, with a regular coordinate system within each zone. The false easting refers to the assigned value of 500,000 meters to the central meridian to avoid negative coordinates.

text: Which of the following is a demographic factor that determines mortality?
explanation: All listed factors are demographic factors that can influence mortality rates.

text: In which of the following ways does the quantitative revolution contributed to the development of geography?
options: By advocating the idea that physical factors should be investigated from different perspectives.
By integrating the idea that geography can be used to solve socioeconomic and political problems.
By integrating statistical techniques, spatial reasoning and digital system in geographical research.
Through formulating theory such as human beings can change their environment using the latest technology.
correctAnswer: By integrating statistical techniques, spatial reasoning and digital system in geographical research.
explanation: Quantitative revolution introduced statistical and digital methods to geography.

text: Which of the following is NOT typically considered a source of social change?
options: Political revolutions, characterized by mass mobilization, ideological shifts, and institutional reforms, challenging established power structures and social hierarchies.
Economic shifts, encompassing fluctuations in market dynamics, wealth distribution, and employment patterns, influence consumption habits and lifestyle choices.
Religious doctrines, guiding moral principles, ethical norms, and social behaviours, shape individual identities and community practices across diverse cultural contexts.

Geographic factors, including topographical features, climatic conditions, and spatial distributions, may influence settlement patterns and resource availability but do not directly drive social change.
correctAnswer: Geographic factors, including topographical features, climatic conditions, and spatial distributions, may influence settlement patterns and resource availability but do not directly drive social change.
explanation: Geographic factors influence but do not directly drive social change.

text: What characterizes the coniferous forest region of the earth?
options: Winter is a period of long days of bright sunshine in the region.
The region receives a high amount of rainfall throughout the year.
Agriculture is the most important economic activity of the region.
The region is dominated by a single type of plant species.
correctAnswer: The region is dominated by a single type of plant species.
explanation: Coniferous forests are dominated by cone-bearing evergreen trees like pine, spruce, and fir. These forests have low biodiversity compared to other forest biomes, with relatively few dominant tree species adapted to cold temperatures and acidic soils in the northern latitudes (taiga or boreal forests).

text: Which one of the following is a demographic factor that determines mortality?
explanation: All listed factors are demographic factors that can influence mortality rates.

text: What kind of mining technique is mainly used to extract coal and metal near the surface of the ground?
explanation: Open pit mining is used for near-surface mineral deposits.

text: Which one of the following is true about wave theory of EMR EXCEPT one?
options: The wavelength is directly proportional to frequency.
The longer the wavelength, the lower the frequency
Wavelength is normally measured in hertz (Hz)
correctAnswer: The wavelength is directly proportional to frequency.
explanation: Wavelength is inversely proportional to frequency, not directly proportional. The relationship is defined by the equation c = λf, where c is the speed of light, λ is wavelength, and f is frequency.

text: Why is geographic research different from the other research types? Geographic research focuses on
options: the social challenges from a temporal point of view.
the cause-effect relationships of different phenomena.
the geological formation through mathematical modeling.
the factors that affect the spatial distribution of population.
correctAnswer: the factors that affect the spatial distribution of population.
explanation: Geography uniquely studies spatial distributions and patterns, analyzing how physical and human phenomena vary across space and the relationships between location and various factors. This spatial perspective distinguishes geographic research from other disciplines that may focus on temporal, causal, or purely physical relationships without the spatial dimension.

text: Which one of the following is a desired outcome of households which pursue sustainable livelihood strategy?
explanation: None of the options reflect a desired outcome of sustainable livelihood strategies. Sustainable livelihood strategies aim to achieve enhanced well-being, increased income, reduced inequality, and improved food security while maintaining environmental sustainability.

text: Identify the incorrect statement about map projection.
options: It is a combination of scale alternation and a system of transformation of the curved surface to flat surface
It is the methods by which the spherical shape of a part or the entire surface of the earth is transformed onto a flat surface
It is a process of transforming three-dimensional earth's features into a two-dimensional model without any distortion
It is a process of transforming geographic coordinates into plane coordinates
correctAnswer: It is a process of transforming three-dimensional earth's features into a two-dimensional model without any distortion
explanation: The statement about transforming into a two-dimensional model without distortion is incorrect.

text: _____________ is a type of food insecurity which occurs when there is a regular pattern of inadequate access to food.
explanation: Chronic food insecurity refers to a consistent lack of access to food over time.

text: Which one of the following statement is incorrect about geographic coordinate system?
options: It uses a three-dimensional spherical surface to define locations on the earth
Latitude values are measured relative to the equator and range from – 90° at the south pole to +90° at the north pole
Although longitude and latitude can locate exact positions on the surface of the globe, they are not uniform units of measure
correctAnswer: Although longitude and latitude can locate exact positions on the surface of the globe, they are not uniform units of measure
explanation: The incorrect statement is option D. Longitude and latitude ARE uniform units of measure in a geographic coordinate system (measured in degrees). The non-uniform aspect is that the distance represented by one degree of longitude varies with latitude (becoming smaller as you move from the equator toward the poles).

text: Identify the last step in the cartographic communication process.
explanation: Map interpretation is the final step in the cartographic communication process, where users derive meaning from the map by connecting the information presented with their existing knowledge. This follows map reading and analysis.

text: Which among the following is not related to GIS software?
explanation: STAAD Pro is not a GIS software; it is used for structural analysis.

text: A type of map that shows detailed information about their subjects refers to:
explanation: Thematic maps are designed to show specific themes or detailed information about particular subjects, unlike general purpose maps which show a variety of features.

text: Which one of the following is not true about projected coordinate system?
explanation: The option 'All' is not true as it implies that all previous statements are characteristics of projected coordinate systems, which is incorrect. Projected coordinate systems are two-dimensional representations that convert spherical coordinates to a flat surface.

text: What is the areal scale equivalence of scale 5cm to 25km?
explanation: The correct area scale equivalence is 25cm² to 625km².

text: What does high drainage density imply in terms of the texture of the drainage?
explanation: High drainage density typically indicates a fine drainage texture.

text: ______________ is an indicator of food security revealed through adequate diet, clean water, sanitation and health care to reach a state of nutritional well-being where all physiological needs are met.
explanation: Utilization refers to the proper use of food and resources to achieve food security.

text: Which one of the following IS NOT TRUE about development geography?
options: It studies spatial patterns in development
It seeks to understand both the geographical causes and consequences of varying development
It studies the spatial distribution of economic activities on the surface of the earth
explanation: All statements about development geography are true.

text: Which one of the following statement is not correct about map?
options: A map is a three-dimensional representation of the earth's surface
Maps show the earth's surface as bird's-eye view
All maps are smaller than the area they represent
Maps are simplified representations of reality
correctAnswer: A map is a three-dimensional representation of the earth's surface
explanation: Maps are two-dimensional representations, not three-dimensional.

text: Which type of shock is the death of a working household member?
explanation: The death of a working household member is an idiosyncratic shock, which affects individual households rather than entire communities. Covariate shocks affect multiple households or communities simultaneously (like droughts or floods).

text: A step of map making processes executed first is:
explanation: Organization and manipulation of data is typically the first step in the map-making process, followed by design and preparation, then reproduction and production.

text: According to Household Hunger Scale, which one of the following Household Hunger Score does show severe hunger in the Household Hunger Category?
explanation: A score of 7 - 9 indicates severe hunger according to the Household Hunger Scale.

text: What type of drainage pattern is characterized by both the main stream and its tributaries displaying right-angled bends?
explanation: The rectangular drainage pattern is characterized by right-angled bends.

text: Which one of the following is not a characteristic of graphic generalization in cartographic generalization?
explanation: Enlargement is not a characteristic of graphic generalization.

text: A rational database contains ________.
explanation: A relational database (not 'rational') can contain both numbers and texts, which are organized in tables with rows and columns. Modern relational databases can also store other data types, but numbers and text are the fundamental data types.

text: Which one of the following is true about 'unbalanced growth model'?
options: It advocates simultaneous growth of all sectors of the economy
It requires a lot of capital investment right from the beginning of the growth process
It is a long period strategy of growth
It requires relatively much less investment
correctAnswer: It requires relatively much less investment
explanation: The unbalanced growth model suggests that it requires relatively less investment in some sectors.

text: ____________ is food security measurement technique which is used as a means of measuring the status of food security at household and individual level.
explanation: The Household Hunger Scale is specifically designed to measure food security at the household level.

text: Which of the following provides opportunities to acquire spatial information for map making?
explanation: All the listed options—aerial photography, satellite imagery, and GPS—provide methods to acquire spatial information for map making. These technologies are complementary and often used together in modern cartography to gather comprehensive spatial data.

text: What is a Digital Elevation Model (DEM)?
options: A survey based on field notes and measurements
A raster-based digital dataset of topography
A classification system for terrain features
A technique for mapping underwater terrain
correctAnswer: A raster-based digital dataset of topography
explanation: A Digital Elevation Model (DEM) is a raster-based digital dataset representing topography.

text: A type of thematic map that portrays the relief features of the land by hatchers, or columnar or by different shades or tints (green, yellow, and brown) between the contour lines refers to:
explanation: Chorographic maps depict relief features using various shades and tints.

text: Identify a type of map projection based on developable surface used.
explanation: Cylindrical projections are based on developable surfaces.

text: Among the following ____________ can be expressed as an example of hardware component.
explanation: A keyboard is a hardware component, while the others are software.

text: ___________ comprises the capabilities, assets and activities required for a means of living.
explanation: Livelihood refers to the means of securing the necessities of life.

text: If the angular bearing of point A to point B is 135°, then the cardinal direction will be:
explanation: An angular bearing of 135° corresponds to the southeast direction.

text: When crossing a ridge at right angles, what is the typical experience in terms of elevation?
options: Climbing steeply to the crest and then descending steeply to the base
Walking along a level path with no noticeable slope
Gradually ascending along the ridge with a gentle incline
Descending sharply from the crest and then ascending gradually to the base
correctAnswer: Climbing steeply to the crest and then descending steeply to the base
explanation: Typically, one would climb steeply to the crest and then descend steeply.

text: Which one of the following concepts best defines development?
explanation: Development is a multidimensional process that includes economic growth along with improvements in human well-being, reduction in inequality, and sustainability. Simple growth alone does not fully define development.

text: What is the current scope of cartography?
explanation: The current scope of cartography extends beyond simple map making to include data collection, visualization, analysis, and interpretation of spatial information in various digital and physical formats.

text: Identify the real model of the earth.
explanation: Both spheroid and ellipsoid are models of the earth.

text: By 'spatial data' we mean data that has:
explanation: Spatial data refers to data that has positional values.

text: It is a process of transforming geographic coordinates into plane coordinates.
explanation: Correspondence relations in cartography refer to the mathematical transformation of geographic coordinates (latitude and longitude) into plane coordinates (x, y) for representation on a flat map. This process involves map projections which inherently cause some distortion of area, shape, distance, or direction.

text: According to Rostow's stages of economic growth, in which stage do new technologies and capital get applied and production is greatly increased?
explanation: The 'Take off' stage is characterized by significant increases in production.

text: At which map scale are terrain components shown in detailed terrain classification maps?
explanation: Detailed terrain classification maps are typically at a scale of 1:10,000.

text: If a family sends children to relatives' or friends' homes, what type of coping strategy is it?
explanation: Sending children to relatives is a livelihood-based coping strategy.

text: Which one of the following statement is correct about globe?
options: It is a three-dimensional model with more than half of its surface observed at a time
It represents the earth and its other features in their true shape
Distances between any two points are correctly maintained on globe
The longitudes and latitudes are so arranged that it is convenient to locate any point with ease and precision
correctAnswer: It represents the earth and its other features in their true shape
explanation: A globe accurately represents the earth and its features in true shape.

text: Which one of the following is not a significance of a map?
options: Identifying locations, distance, area and direction
explanation: While maps can and do support development planning (making this a significant use of maps), the question is asking for which option is NOT a significance. However, all listed options ARE significant uses of maps. This question may have an error in its formulation.

text: The process of capturing satellite image is called _______.
explanation: All terms refer to the process of capturing satellite images.

text: How can you determine the direction of water flow in a valley?
options: By looking at the contour lines and determining if they form a U or V shape
By looking at the closed end of the contour line, which always points upstream
By observing the direction of the highest ground surrounding the valley
By determining the location of the lowest ground within the valley
correctAnswer: By looking at the closed end of the contour line, which always points upstream
explanation: The closed end of the contour line points upstream, indicating the direction of water flow.

text: A type of data that are grouped in classes according to differences in type is:
explanation: Qualitative data is categorized based on types or characteristics.

text: Which one of the following is true about agricultural resources of Africa?
options: It is the backbone of the economy of many African countries
Animal production absorbs much of the continent's labor force
Africa is rich in terms of certain tropical crops such as coffee, cocoa, tea, sugarcane, cotton
explanation: Both statements A and C are true regarding Africa's agricultural resources.

text: Which of the following is true about Africa's position in relation to other landmasses and water bodies?
options: Africa is located south of Europe and west of the Indian Ocean.
Africa is located north of Europe and east of the Atlantic Ocean.
Africa is located southwest of Asia and south of the Mediterranean Sea.
Africa is located north of the Southern Ocean and west of the Indian Ocean.
correctAnswer: Africa is located south of Europe and west of the Indian Ocean.
explanation: Africa is indeed located south of Europe and west of the Indian Ocean.

text: Which one of the following statements explains a market economy?
options: It is entirely state-owned economic activity
It is free from tax and government control
It encourages and promotes private ownership
It controls all production and distribution
correctAnswer: It encourages and promotes private ownership
explanation: A market economy primarily encourages and promotes private ownership of resources and means of production. It operates based on the principles of demand and supply with limited government intervention, unlike state-owned or command economies.

text: Which one of the following IS NOT TRUE about Africa's location?
options: Africa lies between 37° 21'N and 34° 52'S latitudes and between 17° 33'W and 51° 28'E longitudes
Africa stretches in all the four hemispheres
The equator crosses Africa at its northern part
Africa is found to the north of the South Sea
correctAnswer: The equator crosses Africa at its northern part
explanation: The equator crosses Africa at its center, not its northern part.

text: Which one is the largest sub-physiographic region in the Northwestern Highlands of the Horn?
explanation: The Shewan plateau is the largest sub-physiographic region in the Northwestern Highlands.

text: Which one of the drainage systems of Africa is the largest in terms of catchment area, annual discharge, and drainage density?
explanation: The Atlantic Ocean drainage system is the largest in Africa.

text: Which one of the following best describes the advantages of Africa's large size?
options: Huge resource potentials in terms of resources
correctAnswer: Huge resource potentials in terms of resources
explanation: Africa's large size provides significant resource potential.

text: Which one of the following concepts describes the concept of globalization?
options: Economic, political and cultural interactions of countries in the world
An act of enabling countries of the world to exchange in single currency
A means to achieve world peace and security through military force
A process that deals with challenges of global climate change
correctAnswer: Economic, political and cultural interactions of countries in the world
explanation: Globalization encompasses economic, political, and cultural interactions.

text: Which of the following makes up the majority of Africa's relief?
explanation: Plateaus make up the majority of Africa's relief.

text: Which one of the following is true about the advantage of Africa's shape?
options: It determines the socioeconomic integration and flow of goods and services within the region
It provides geographical accessibility to the rest of the world
It allows Africa to have a large land area for settlements and economic activities
It makes geographical connectivity difficult among the people of the region
correctAnswer: It determines the socioeconomic integration and flow of goods and services within the region
explanation: Africa's shape influences socioeconomic integration and the flow of goods.

text: Which branch of the East African Rift where the Western and Eastern Branches converge?
options: Ethio - Eritrea - Djibouti - Northern Somalia Branch
correctAnswer: Ethio - Eritrea - Djibouti - Northern Somalia Branch
explanation: The Ethio - Eritrea - Djibouti - Northern Somalia Branch is where the Western and Eastern branches converge.

text: Which one of the following is the characteristics of traditional economic system?
options: Lack of knowledge of science and technology
Low level of exchange of goods
explanation: Traditional economic systems often lack technological knowledge and have low levels of exchange.

text: Which one of the following major geologic events occurred in Africa during the Cenozoic Era?
options: Formation of the Great East African Rift valley
Formation of many of the volcanic mountains
Climatic change and Pluvial rains in tropical Africa
explanation: All listed events occurred during the Cenozoic Era in Africa.

text: Which part of the spectrum is better recommended for vegetation dynamics analysis?
explanation: Infrared, particularly near-infrared (NIR), is commonly used for analyzing vegetation dynamics because healthy vegetation strongly reflects NIR radiation while absorbing visible light for photosynthesis. This property makes infrared ideal for calculating vegetation indices like NDVI.

text: Which technique is used to interpret terrain features by analyzing the spatial arrangement of features?
explanation: Spatial analysis interprets terrain features based on their arrangement. It examines the relationships, patterns, and distributions of geographic features to understand landscape characteristics and processes.

text: In cartography, the stage at which information and messages are conveyed is known as?
explanation: Map design is the stage where information is conveyed.

text: Which one of the electromagnetic spectrums is our eyes - our 'remote sensors' - can detect?
explanation: Human eyes can only detect the visible spectrum of light, which ranges approximately from 380 to 750 nanometers in wavelength.

text: Which of the following is NOT a terrain feature?
explanation: A city is not a natural terrain feature.

text: The Solow - Swan Model of Economic Growth suggests that long - run economic growth is determined by:
explanation: The model emphasizes savings and investment as key to long-run growth.

text: Which of the following is NOT an analytical approach used in land use planning and evaluation?
explanation: All listed options are analytical approaches used in land use planning.

text: How does the sustainable livelihoods framework align with rights - based approaches?
options: By focusing on market - driven solutions
By ensuring access to basic human rights
